event_description: Norfolk Naval Station: Largest naval base in the world. Home port for carrier strike groups.

Bahrain (5th Fleet): 5th Fleet HQ. Direct control of Gulf naval assets. Day 96 (June 3): Bahrain's army intercepted three Iranian ballistic missiles and several drones; the IRGC claimed strikes on the 5th Fleet HQ, an airbase, and helicopters, which CENTCOM denied as false. The US naval blockade of Iranian ports ended May 29 (Trump announcement) — the dual Gulf blockade is now eased on the US side, though Iran's selective Hormuz closure persists. Day 98 (June 5): Bahrain intercepted 3 Iranian ballistic missiles plus several drones in Iran's June 5 salvo (all intercepted, no casualties); CENTCOM also downed IRGC drones near Hormuz over June 5-6. Day 103 (June 10): Iran struck again in retaliation for the June 9 US strikes — the IRGC launched drones at the US Fifth Fleet HQ; Bahrain's defenses intercepted/repelled them with no US casualties or damage reported (IRGC battle-damage claims UNVERIFIED and US-disputed). Day 110 (June 17): No new strikes on US bases June 11-17; the released 14-point MOU commits the US to lift the naval blockade on the June 19 signing and to withdraw forces 'from surrounding areas' within 30 days of a final agreement, though a June 15 US advisory says the blockade remains in effect until the signing). Day 121 (June 28): TARGETED AGAIN — the IRGC fired missiles and drones at US 5th Fleet / NSA Bahrain in retaliation for the June 26-27 US strikes on Iranian territory; an 8-story residential building in Muharraq was hit and its top floor destroyed (no deaths), and Bahrain's FM called it a 'dangerous escalation.' The IRGC claimed 8 US military sites struck; a US official said no intended targets were impacted. A 'stand down for now' followed June 28-29. The US 60-day Iran oil sanctions waiver (General License X) remains valid through Aug 21. Day 137 (July 7-14): CEASEFIRE COLLAPSED — sirens sounded at NSA Bahrain/Juffair three times (Jul 8, 12, 13) as Iran resumed missile/drone waves; the IRGC claimed strikes on the 5th Fleet HQ area and Sheikh Isa AB as part of its '80+/85 US sites' response (claims UNVERIFIED); downed drones damaged Bahraini homes; NO confirmed US casualties (CENTCOM). Day 147 (July 24): the IRGC CLAIMED heavy damage to the US Fifth Fleet HQ watchtower in its 27th wave of Operation Nasr-2 — UNVERIFIED and denied by the absence of any CENTCOM confirmation, echoing its false June 3 claim. Day 150 (July 27): no US strikes for a fourth day as the mutual pause held; the naval blockade of Iranian ports continued to be run from here.

Prince Sultan AB (Saudi Arabia): Key US/coalition air base in the Kingdom. Day 68-69 (May 6-7): Saudi Arabia suspended US base/airspace access for Project Freedom (NBC News May 6 / AP May 7); 43 aircraft (13 KC-135, 6 E-3G AWACS) reportedly grounded during the 4-day suspension per House of Saud / Al-Monitor satellite imagery. Day 70-71 (May 7-8): Restrictions LIFTED after a second Trump–MBS phone call (WSJ, Türkiye Today, The Defense News May 8). WSJ: Pentagon could resume Project Freedom 'as early as this week.' Anonymous Saudi source to Al-Hadath: Kingdom 'did not allow the use of its airspace to support offensive military operations' — public Saudi line at variance with WSJ characterization (PARTIAL-CONFIRM). Major precedent for real-time GCC ABO leverage. Day 137 REGIONAL (July 13): the Houthi-Saudi truce (since March 2022) BROKE — after alleged strikes on Sanaa International Airport (aimed at blocking an Iranian air bridge), Yemen's Houthis fired missiles at Saudi Arabia's Abha airport, their first attack on the kingdom in over four years, declaring the 'de-escalation phase' over; Houthis also warned airlines off Saudi airspace.

Ali Al Salem AB (Kuwait): 386th Air Expeditionary Wing hub. Day 68-69 (May 6-7): Kuwait restricted overflight for offensive Project Freedom-related operations (NBC News May 6); Camp Arifjan houses largest US troop concentration in Middle East and ARCENT forward HQ. Day 70-71 (May 7-8): RESTRICTIONS LIFTED — Kuwaiti overflight restored after diplomatic intercession (WSJ; Drop Site News). Day 72 dawn (May 10) preview: Kuwait MoD (Brig. Gen. Saud Abdulaziz Al-Otaibi) reported armed forces 'detected and dealt with several hostile drones within Kuwaiti airspace.' Day 89-90 (May 27-28): Kuwait REACTIVATED air defenses — Kuwaiti forces INTERCEPTED an Iranian ballistic missile fired at Kuwait at 10:17 p.m. ET May 27 (CENTCOM called it an 'egregious ceasefire violation'); Kuwait's army said it was 'responding to hostile missile and drone threats' and the Foreign Ministry condemned the 'sinful Iranian attacks.' The IRGC claimed it had struck a U.S. air base in Kuwait in retaliation for U.S. strikes near Bandar Abbas. REGIONAL (May 28): Treasury Sec. Scott Bessent threatened Oman with sanctions if it facilitates Hormuz tolls. Day 95-96 (June 2-3): Iran struck Kuwait again — a June 3 drone/missile strike on Kuwait International Airport killed one Indian national and wounded 63+, briefly closing a terminal; Kuwait's Defense Ministry said it destroyed 12+ missiles and ~12 drones over June 2-3, and Kuwait expelled two Iranian diplomats. Day 98 (June 5): Kuwait intercepted 7 Iranian ballistic missiles in the June 5 salvo launched after the US coastal-radar strikes at Qeshm and Goruk (all intercepted, no casualties). Day 103 (June 10): the IRGC launched drones at Ali Al Salem Air Base in retaliation for the June 9 US strikes; all intercepted, no casualties or damage reported. Day 117 (June 24): US Embassy Kuwait REOPENED — operations resumed at midnight June 24 (Secretary of State Rubio held a flag-raising during a Gulf tour of the UAE, Kuwait and Bahrain) after the March suspension caused by Iranian drone attacks; this is a re-establishment, not a drawdown. NO US troop withdrawal has begun — per the MOU text, the US obligation to remove its forces from the proximity of Iran triggers only 'within 30 days after the final Deal,' and no final Deal yet exists (the 60-day negotiation window runs from June 17), so the withdrawal clock has not started. Carriers Lincoln and Bush remain on station in the Arabian Sea; VP Vance said IRGC and US military reps would be posted in Doha as a de-confliction channel. Day 121 (June 28): TARGETED AGAIN — the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at Ali Al Salem AB in retaliation for the June 26-27 US strikes on Iranian territory; Kuwait intercepted 2 ballistic missiles with no damage. A 'stand down for now' followed June 28-29; the withdrawal clock still has not started (no final Deal exists). Day 137 (July 7-14): CEASEFIRE COLLAPSED — IRGC-claimed strikes on Ali Al Salem AB (and Camp Arifjan) Jul 8-13; Kuwait's army engaged 'hostile aerial targets'; IRGC claimed 2 HIMARS launchers destroyed (UNVERIFIED by Kuwait/US); no confirmed damage or US casualties. Iran also struck a Kuwaiti offshore oil platform and 3 northern border posts Jul 12 (1 worker injured). Day 146 (July 17-18): Iranian Shahed drones and missiles struck two Kuwaiti power+desalination plants near Mina Abdullah, setting them ablaze on consecutive days (firefighters and a worker injured); Kuwait relies on desalination for ~90% of its drinking water (CNN geolocated a Shahed striking a warehouse near Mina Abdullah). Iran is now striking host-nation CIVILIAN infrastructure, not only US bases. Day 147 (July 24): the IRGC CLAIMED to have destroyed an ammunition depot here, with US casualties, during its 27th wave of Operation Nasr-2 — UNVERIFIED. CENTCOM did not confirm that any facility or person was hit, and Euronews reported the US has not confirmed its facilities or personnel were targeted. Attribute strictly to the IRGC.

Azraq AB / Muwaffaq Salti (Jordan): Hosts US Air Forces Central's 323rd Air Expeditionary Wing (~3,800 troops); reported to host MQ-9 Reapers and has supported F-16/F-35 operations; ~60 miles (100km) NE of Amman. Day 103 (June 10): TARGETED for the first time in the war — Iran fired long-range ballistic missiles at Azraq, the war's DEEPEST Iranian reach (~1,000km from the Iranian coast), in retaliation for the June 9 US strikes; Jordan intercepted 5 missiles (debris only, no casualties). The IRGC claimed (UNVERIFIED, US-disputed) it destroyed an F-35 hangar at Azraq. Day 137 (July 12-14): TARGETED AGAIN — Iran claimed strikes on a US command-and-control center and drone hangars in the Prince Hassan AB / Azraq area; Jordan repeatedly reported intercepting 4 missiles entering its airspace from Iran (Jul 12-14), with shrapnel falling in several areas; no casualties (Jordan Armed Forces / Petra). Day 146 (July 17): DEADLIEST SINGLE STRIKE ON US FORCES IN THE WAR — an Iranian ballistic-missile attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base killed 3 US soldiers (1st Lt. Tyler Feehan, Pvt. Isabella Gonzales, Sgt. Angel Rampersad) and medevac'd 4; the base had been used to launch US strikes on Iran. A 4th soldier died Jul 18 in northern Iraq; Trump attended the Dover dignified transfer of four fallen Jul 22. The IRGC also claimed a Jul 18 strike on Azraq destroying ≥5 US aircraft (UNVERIFIED, US-disputed) and incited Jordanians to attack US troops. Iran is now striking host-nation civilian infrastructure, not only US bases. Day 140 (July 17): an Iranian ballistic-missile strike hit a barracks here, killing 3 US soldiers — 1st Lt. Tyler James Feehan (25), Pvt. Isabella Gonzales (19) and Sgt. Angel S. Rampersad (28); Trump attended the dignified transfer at Dover on July 22. Day 147 (July 24): named among the targets of the IRGC's 27th wave of Operation Nasr-2, which struck 'sites in Jordan' — no damage confirmed by CENTCOM.
RAF Fairford: UK. B-52 forward deployment for CENTCOM operations.
Pentagon: DoD HQ. Where Operation Epic Fury is commanded.
New York: NYSE/NYMEX. Processing war-driven market volatility.
Houston: US energy capital. Refinery hub feeling Hormuz closure.

Camp Arifjan (Kuwait): US Army Central (ARCENT) forward HQ; largest US troop concentration in the Middle East. Day 137 (July 8): NAMED A TARGET for the first time — the IRGC named Camp Arifjan (with Ali Al Salem AB) among targets of its Jul 8 missile/drone response, claiming HIMARS launchers and ammunition depots were hit; claims UNVERIFIED by Kuwait/US, no confirmed damage or US casualties (Kuwait General Staff / CENTCOM).

Kuwait offshore oil platform: Offshore oil drilling platform in Kuwaiti territorial waters. Day 137 (July 12): STRUCK by Iran — 1 worker injured, with material damage also reported at 3 northern Kuwaiti border posts (Kuwait Defense Ministry, Col. Saud Abdulaziz Al-Atwan). First strike on Kuwaiti offshore energy infrastructure of the war; helped drive the Jul 13 oil-price spike (Brent +9.59%).

Oman radar sites (Musandam / Al Wusta): Long-range / vessel-detection radar sites in Oman's Musandam and Al Wusta governorates. Day 137 (July 12): IRGC-claimed drone strikes — damage claimed by the IRGC (UNVERIFIED); Oman summoned Iran's ambassador in protest (Oman Foreign Ministry).

Bab el-Mandeb (Houthi Red Sea blockade): Southern Red Sea chokepoint — ~14 miles wide at its narrowest (~40% narrower than Hormuz); ~6.2M bbl/day of oil transited over the past month (Kpler via CNN). Day 143-145 (July 20-22): NEW FRONT — the Houthis declared (Jul 20) and enforced (Jul 22) a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, striking the Saudi tankers Encelia (bow fire confirmed, SPA) and Layla (unconfirmed) and claiming they forced ~10 ships to retreat. This opened a second chokepoint front, put Bab el-Mandeb transit at risk, and helped push Brent toward $100 intraday Jul 23; five tankers had already changed course by Jul 22. Trump said the US would 'hold Iran responsible' for the Houthi attacks.

Jizan Aramco Refinery (Saudi Arabia): Saudi Aramco refinery, 400,000 bpd. Day 148 (July 25): STRUCK BY THE HOUTHIS — ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones set the refinery alight; a large smoke plume and a NASA FIRMS thermal anomaly at ~01:17 UTC confirm the fire. Saudi Arabia and Aramco issued no official damage or casualty assessment. It was the first Houthi strike on Saudi oil facilities since 2022 (spokesman Yahya Saree), announced as retaliation for Saudi-led coalition strikes on Hodeidah and Kamaran Island on July 24.

Yanbu Oil Terminal (Saudi Arabia): Saudi Arabia's primary Hormuz-bypass export hub on the Red Sea — handled ~92% of Saudi seaborne crude exports in June 2026 (Kpler/AFP), with loadings hitting a record 4.7M bpd around July 13 (Signal Ocean). Day 148 (July 25): TARGETED BY THE HOUTHIS — two ballistic missiles aimed at Aramco installations were intercepted by a Patriot battery operated by the GREEK military in Saudi Arabia; no damage reported. The attack demonstrates Houthi reach against the one corridor absorbing Hormuz's throttling, raising the prospect of a dual-chokepoint squeeze.

Erbil (Iraq) — US-hosting base: US-hosting installation in Iraqi Kurdistan. Day 141 (July 18): a strike on the Komala opposition facility killed ~9. Day 142 (July 19): Staff Sgt. Michael Emmanuel Swinton was killed in a drone detonation at Erbil, one of the four US deaths restored to the Pentagon casualty rolls on July 26. Day 147 (July 24): explosions and black smoke near the base were confirmed by an AP photo (Stella Martany) during the IRGC's 27th wave of Operation Nasr-2 — the only independent corroboration of that salvo; CENTCOM did not confirm any facility or person was hit.

Camp Udairi / Camp Buehring (Kuwait): US Army training and staging complex in northern Kuwait. Day 147 (July 24): the IRGC CLAIMED to have destroyed 3 ammunition and equipment hangars here in its 27th wave of Operation Nasr-2 — UNVERIFIED, sourced only to Iranian state media and IRGC statements; CENTCOM did not confirm that any facility or person was hit, and Euronews reported the US has not confirmed its facilities or personnel were targeted.

Isa AB / Sheikh Isa (Bahrain): Bahraini air base hosting rotational US aircraft. Day 147 (July 24): the IRGC CLAIMED Arash kamikaze-drone hits on fuel tanks and barracks here during its 27th wave of Operation Nasr-2 — UNVERIFIED, attributed to IRGC statements and Iranian state media only; CENTCOM issued no confirmation of damage or casualties.

strike_notes: Day 170 (August 16, Sunday): STILL ON STATION, RELIEF INBOUND. The Lincoln remains on station in the Arabian Sea after a record 240+ consecutive days at sea, extended well past its original May return date to sustain Iran operations, but is now slated for relief by the USS George Washington (CVN-73), which has begun sailing from the western Pacific. AP (Aug 15) reported growing mental-health and supply/logistics strain aboard and congressional scrutiny, with Democratic lawmakers calling for investigations; Trump (Aug 14) said the record time at sea was 'not nearly long enough.' PRIOR — Day 157 (August 3, Monday): DISPOSITION HELD; STILL UNRELIEVED THROUGH A STRIKE CYCLE AND A STAND-DOWN. No repositioning is confirmed for July 28-August 3. The last independent fixes are USNI's Fleet & Marine Tracker (July 27) and The War Zone's carrier tracker (July 28), both placing the Lincoln CSG on station in the Arabian Sea supporting Operation Epic Fury; NO August 3 USNI weekly was reviewed for this cycle, so treat position, escort composition and readiness as CARRIED FORWARD rather than freshly verified, and re-verify against the next USNI edition. The window itself was busy: Iran's attempted missile attack on July 28 broke the pause, CENTCOM answered with a 'heavy wave' completed 10 p.m. ET July 29 using air- and sea-launched precision munitions, Iran struck Jordan and Kuwait July 30, and the IRGC claimed two Hormuz tanker strikes July 31 (unverified). CENTCOM did not attribute the July 29 wave to specific platforms, so no strike role is asserted here. Trump then canceled a planned major strike on Iranian energy infrastructure late August 1 and said August 3 that talks would begin, with US forces described as remaining 'locked and loaded.' READINESS FLAG — Lincoln has NOT been relieved. Its record run stood at 207+ consecutive days at sea as of the last verified count, past USS Dwight D. Eisenhower's 206-day 2020 record (Ike and San Jacinto returned to Norfolk August 9-10, 2020, having first broken the old 160-day mark at 161 days on June 25, 2020), and no relief-in-place has been reported. Every additional week compounds maintenance and crew-fatigue risk; a relief-in-place would itself be a major naval-disposition event and should be treated as a watch item each cycle. Escort composition unchanged and unverified in-window: DESRON 21 screen of USS Spruance (DDG-111) and USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. (DDG-121). Blockade 2.0 continues — 20 commercial vessels redirected as of July 29, 2 disabled kinetically, 2 boarded (UANI/CENTCOM). PRIOR — Day 150 (July 27, Monday): RECORD DEPLOYMENT CONTINUES THROUGH THE STRIKE PAUSE. USNI's Fleet & Marine Tracker (Jul 27) places the Lincoln CSG on station in the Arabian Sea, unchanged from Jul 20. Lincoln has now passed 207 consecutive days at sea, breaking USS Dwight D. Eisenhower's 2020 record for the longest continuous stretch at sea by a US carrier (Stars and Stripes; TWZ Jul 20), with CVW-9 embarked. CENTCOM completed its 13th consecutive night of strikes at 9 p.m. ET July 23 and announced none July 24-27; Iran halted retaliation after its July 24 IRGC salvo, and the mutual pause has held three days. The carrier's mission did not pause with the strikes: the naval blockade of Iranian ports continues, with CENTCOM counting 12 commercial vessels redirected, 2 disabled and 2 boarded as of July 26. No escort composition changes were verified Jul 21-27. PRIOR — Day 137 (July 14, Tuesday): COMBAT STRIKE OPERATIONS RESUMED — the ceasefire collapsed July 7 (Iran fired on 3 Hormuz-area tankers; Trump declared the ceasefire 'over' July 8) and CENTCOM ran five-plus strike waves against 300+ Iranian targets July 7-14. USNI Fleet Tracker (Jul 13) confirms the Lincoln CSG (CVW-9, DESRON 21) conducting combat strike operations in the Arabian Sea — screen listed as USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. (DDG-121, Air Defense Commander) and USS Spruance (DDG-111); no cruiser listed Jul 13. No confirmed escort additions/removals vs the Jul 6 horizon. Lincoln passed 200 consecutive days at sea on Jun 30 and appeared in the Jun 30 PHOTOEX with Bush and Tripoli. USNI counts ~24+ US warships in the Middle East, including 15 destroyers. Red Sea destroyers: USS Thomas Hudner (DDG-116), USS Gonzalez (DDG-66). PRIOR — Day 122 (June 29, Monday): USNI Fleet & Marine Tracker confirms the Lincoln (CVN-72) CSG still on station in the Arabian Sea — the carrier held position through the June 25-28 re-escalation (four days of US-Iran strikes over Hormuz shipping) with NO surge and NO withdrawal; the DESRON 21 screen includes USS Spruance (DDG-111) and USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. (DDG-121). More than 15,000 US troops and >200 aircraft/warships remain committed to Strait-deterrence and freedom-of-navigation missions (GlobalSecurity Day-122). Day 115 (June 22, Monday): USNI Fleet & Marine Tracker confirms the Lincoln (CVN-72) CSG operating in the Arabian Sea in support of Operation Epic Fury with Carrier Air Wing 9 embarked — 'Tophatters' VFA-14, 'Black Aces' VFA-41, 'Vigilantes' VFA-151, VMFA-314 (F-35C), VAQ-133 and VAW-117; co-located with the Bush (CVN-77) CSG in the 5th Fleet AOR. event_description: Minab: IRGC Navy 'Sayyid al-Shuhada' military complex / Asif missile brigade HQ (intended target)
strike_notes: Deadliest confirmed civilian casualty incident of the war. Struck at approximately 10:45 AM local time on Day 1 during opening wave. School was triple-tapped per Iranian officials (mayor of Minab, Ministry of Education). Victims were primarily girls aged 7–12, plus teachers, parents, and the school principal. School had been physically separated from adjacent IRGC naval base by a wall and separate entrance since ~2016, with a visible soccer pitch in the courtyard by 2017 (confirmed by satellite imagery reviewed by HRW, NYT, CNN, TIME). Bellingcat and BBC Verify geolocated footage of a US Tomahawk cruise missile striking the area. Eight munitions experts confirmed to the Washington Post the missile was a Tomahawk. Pentagon preliminary internal investigation found US was likely responsible due to outdated DIA intelligence that failed to distinguish the school from the military compound. CNN reported CENTCOM created target coordinates using outdated DIA information. Trump initially blamed Iran; munitions experts confirmed no Iranian missile matches the weapon in verified footage. US is the only belligerent operating Tomahawk missiles. Under formal Pentagon investigation expected to take months.

Iraq declares neutrality — closes airspace to US combat operations: Iraqi Prime Minister announces Iraq will not be a party to the conflict and orders closure of Iraqi airspace to US combat missions. The declaration creates a legal and diplomatic crisis as US strikes on PMF targets violate the stated neutrality.

event_description: Treasury yields plunge as investors flee to safety: 10-year US Treasury yield drops 28 basis points to 3.92% as global investors flood into US government bonds. The dollar index (DXY) surges 2.1% to 107.8 on safe-haven demand. Gold spikes to $4,850/oz. The flight to safety is the largest single-day move since the early days of COVID-19.

S&P 500 drops 3.1% — worst day since 2024: US stock markets sell off sharply as the full scope of Operation Epic Fury becomes clear. S&P 500 closes at 6,654, down 3.1%. Nasdaq falls 3.8% on tech exposure to global supply chains. Defense stocks (Lockheed Martin, Raytheon, Northrop Grumman) surge 8-12%. Airlines plunge 11%.

Oil surges further as Hormuz closure confirmed: Brent crude closes at $89.20/bbl (+7.2% from yesterday's already elevated close) as markets price in the Strait of Hormuz closure. WTI at $85.40. The combined loss of Iranian exports and Hormuz transit creates a theoretical shortfall of 12+ million barrels per day — the largest supply disruption in oil market history.

strike_notes: Deadliest single strike on Israeli civilians in the conflict. Iranian ballistic missile struck synagogue and public bomb shelter in residential neighborhood, 35km west of Jerusalem. Three Bitton siblings (ages 16, 15, 13) among the dead. United Hatzalah volunteer Ronit Elimelech and her mother Sarah also killed.

event_description: Port Shuaiba, Kuwait: Drone / projectile (under investigation) — 6 US Army Reserve soldiers KIA, multiple wounded
casualties_reported: 6 US Army Reserve soldiers KIA, multiple wounded
strike_notes: Deadliest single attack on US forces in the conflict. Direct hit on makeshift tactical operations center (triple-wide trailer) at civilian port, ~9am local time March 1. One projectile penetrated air defenses. All 6 KIA were from 103rd Sustainment Command (Army Reserve, Des Moines, Iowa): Capt. Cody Khork (35), SFC Nicole Amor (39), SFC Noah Tietjens (42), Sgt. Declan Coady (20), Maj. Jeffrey O'Brien, CWO3 Robert Marzan. Bodies of two initially unaccounted for, recovered from burning building. Dignified transfer at Dover AFB attended by President Trump on March 8.

event_description: Tehran: Leadership House compound (Feb 28, Day 1)
strike_notes: Continuous bombardment since Day 1. Supreme Leader Khamenei killed in initial strike on Leadership House compound along with his daughter, son-in-law, grandchild, and daughter-in-law Zahra Haddad-Adel. Defense Minister Aziz Nasirzadeh, IRGC commander Mohammad Pakpour, chief of staff Abdolrahim Mousavi, Ali Shamkhani, and multiple other senior officials also killed. Mojtaba Khamenei (son) injured but survived; named new Supreme Leader on Mar 8 (Day 9). Day 11 (Mar 10): 40+ killed in Resalat Square residential area strike in eastern Tehran (see tehran-east-residential). Day 12: IDF destroys IRGC Air Force HQ (see tehran-irgc-af-hq). 460+ killed and 4,300+ wounded in Tehran alone as of Day 11 per Tehran Emergency Health Department. Days 20-21: Ali Mohammad Naini (IRGC spokesperson) killed in IAF airstrike overnight Mar 19-20. Day 22: Continued strikes on Tehran military and government infrastructure. Day 24 (Mar 23): IDF launched 'broad wave of attacks' on Tehran. Day 25 (Mar 24): IAF struck 50+ targets overnight. Day 26 (Mar 25): IDF launches 'new wide-scale attacks' on Iranian government infrastructure, including Tehran targets. South Tehran strike kills at least 12, wounds 28. Eastern Tehran strikes destroy school and residential buildings. Day 33 (Apr 1): Airstrike hit former US Embassy compound on Taleghani Street — IRGC-controlled since 1979 — internally detonating penetrator. Russian embassy across the street confirmed blast broke doors/windows at St. Nicholas Orthodox Cathedral and partially collapsed adjacent Russian nursing home.

event_description: Isfahan: Natanz uranium enrichment facility
strike_notes: Primary nuclear targets struck in first wave. Deep penetrating munitions used. Day 22 (Mar 21): Natanz Shahid Ahmadi-Roshan Enrichment Complex struck with bunker-buster bombs (likely GBU-57 MOPs and/or GBU-72 5,000-lb penetrators). Israel denied involvement ('did not conduct any strikes in the area'). IAEA: 'No increase in off-site radiation levels.' DG Grossi called for 'military restraint to avoid any risk of nuclear accident.' Russia condemned as 'blatant violation of international law.' Entrance buildings of underground Fuel Enrichment Plant damaged. Bulk of Iran's enriched uranium (~440 kg) believed at Isfahan, not Natanz. Third strike on Natanz (after June 2025 Operation Midnight Hammer and early March 2026).

event_description: Bushehr: Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant (perimeter and auxiliary buildings)
casualties_reported: Minimal — military targets. No radiation increase per IAEA.
strike_notes: Struck 4 times during Epic Fury (Mar 17, 24, 27, Apr 4). IAEA confirmed no radiation increase. FM Araghchi warned Apr 4 that radioactive release would affect Gulf capitals — Bushehr closer to Kuwait City (175 mi) and Manama (187 mi) than Tehran. Russia's Rosatom evacuating staff (198 additional evacuated Apr 5). Plant holds 72 tons of fuel and 210 tons of spent fuel. IAEA has no inspector access to any Iranian nuclear facility; Iran's parliament suspended IAEA cooperation. Agency has 'lost continuity of knowledge' regarding nuclear material inventories. DAY 57 (Apr 25): 21 consecutive days no new incident; Russia (Rosatom) staff reportedly returning per Russian ambassador statement that Russia hopes work on Bushehr completion will resume soon. DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8 & 14): Bushehr struck again in the renewed campaign; an Iranian official confirmed NO damage to the nuclear power plant (Nour News).

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

DAY 170 UPDATE (Aug 16): IRGC-attributed vessel attacks have continued into mid-August — a UAE/ADNOC tanker hit by missile Aug 8 and two ADNOC tankers drone-struck Aug 13 (0 injuries), plus renewed Houthi Red Sea targeting of Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery Aug 14. event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: Strait of Hormuz (maritime): Anti-ship missiles / drones / naval mines / explosive unmanned surface vessels / coastal batteries — 47+ ships/tugs/rigs hit or near a strike site since Feb 28 (IMO cumulative; +1 with the June 25 Ever Lovely strike); 11 seafarer fatalities to date. weapon_system: Anti-ship missiles / drones / naval mines / explosive unmanned surface vessels / coastal batteries
strike_notes: UKMTO: 20+ confirmed maritime security incidents since Feb 28. Two additional vessels struck Mar 20. Only 21 tankers have crossed the Strait since Feb 28 vs 100+/day pre-war. Half of March transits by shadow fleet (Lloyd's List). Iran selectively allowing passage: India (2 LPG tankers), Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi each transited with individual approval. War risk premiums: 0.125% to ~5% of vessel value (40x increase). $5M per transit for $100M tanker. VLCC rates hit all-time record $423,736/day. GPS/AIS disruption: 44 injected signal zones, 92 denial areas. IMO emergency session Mar 18-19: negotiating safe maritime corridor for seafarer evacuation. UPDATE (June 7): IMO cumulative now 46+ ships/tugs/rigs hit or near a strike site since Feb 28, with 11 seafarer deaths to date; most recently the containership MSC Sariska V was damaged by a drone June 1 at Umm Qasr, Iraq (Manifest §3b). UPDATE (June 25): after the June 17-18 toll-free reopening, the IRGC reasserted permission-only Hormuz transit (VHF Ch.16 warnings) and struck the Singapore-flagged container ship Ever Lovely (bridge damaged, no casualties) ~7.5nm SE of Dahit, Oman — the first ship attack since the reopening (detail under 2026-06-25-hormuz-ever-lovely); 3 tankers turned back and 3 diverted, and the UN IMO paused its plan to evacuate ~11,000 stranded seafarers. Iran is reportedly seeking ~$40B/yr in transit fees once the 60-day free-passage window lapses (WSJ). DAY 170 UPDATE (Aug 16): IRGC-attributed vessel attacks have continued into mid-August — a UAE/ADNOC tanker hit by missile Aug 8 and two ADNOC tankers drone-struck Aug 13 (0 injuries), plus renewed Houthi Red Sea targeting of Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery Aug 14. event_description: Tehran: Leadership House compound (Feb 28, Day 1)
strike_notes: Continuous bombardment since Day 1. Supreme Leader Khamenei killed in initial strike on Leadership House compound along with his daughter, son-in-law, grandchild, and daughter-in-law Zahra Haddad-Adel. Defense Minister Aziz Nasirzadeh, IRGC commander Mohammad Pakpour, chief of staff Abdolrahim Mousavi, Ali Shamkhani, and multiple other senior officials also killed. Mojtaba Khamenei (son) injured but survived; named new Supreme Leader on Mar 8 (Day 9). Day 11 (Mar 10): 40+ killed in Resalat Square residential area strike in eastern Tehran (see tehran-east-residential). Day 12: IDF destroys IRGC Air Force HQ (see tehran-irgc-af-hq). 460+ killed and 4,300+ wounded in Tehran alone as of Day 11 per Tehran Emergency Health Department. Days 20-21: Ali Mohammad Naini (IRGC spokesperson) killed in IAF airstrike overnight Mar 19-20. Day 22: Continued strikes on Tehran military and government infrastructure. Day 24 (Mar 23): IDF launched 'broad wave of attacks' on Tehran. Day 25 (Mar 24): IAF struck 50+ targets overnight. Day 26 (Mar 25): IDF launches 'new wide-scale attacks' on Iranian government infrastructure, including Tehran targets. South Tehran strike kills at least 12, wounds 28. Eastern Tehran strikes destroy school and residential buildings. Day 33 (Apr 1): Airstrike hit former US Embassy compound on Taleghani Street — IRGC-controlled since 1979 — internally detonating penetrator. Russian embassy across the street confirmed blast broke doors/windows at St. Nicholas Orthodox Cathedral and partially collapsed adjacent Russian nursing home.

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: Strait of Hormuz effectively closed. Type: BLOCKADE REIMPOSED & ACTIVELY ENFORCED (effective Jul 14, 20:00 GMT) — the US ran 12 consecutive strike nights through Jul 22-23; as of Jul 20 CENTCOM had redirected 7 vessels and disabled 1 (Belma) under the resumed blockade, 9 redirected by Jul 22; a new Houthi Red Sea blockade of Saudi Arabia (declared Jul 20, enforced Jul 22) opened a second chokepoint front and helped push Brent toward $100 intraday Jul 23. PRIOR: CEASEFIRE COLLAPSED Jul 7 — Iran fired on 3 tankers near the strait in Omani waters (Qatari LNG carrier Al Rekayyat set afire, Saudi crude tanker Wedyan damaged, a third struck by drone); the US called it a 'gross violation' of the June 17 MOU and Trump declared the ceasefire 'over' Jul 8. Five-plus US strike waves hit 300+ Iranian targets Jul 7-14; Iran hit 2 UAE tankers with cruise missiles Jul 13-14 (1 Indian crew member killed). US naval blockade of Iranian ports REIMPOSED effective Jul 14 (20:00 GMT, JMIC). STATUS DISPUTED: Iran declares the strait 'closed'; CENTCOM/JMIC say it remains open via an expanded southern (Omani-coast) route — threat level SEVERE. Transits collapsed ~52% week-on-week (Jul 10-12); just 6 ships Jul 12; ~22 transits in the 24h before the blockade deadline; war-risk premiums rising sharply (Lloyd's List Intelligence). STILL ENFORCED into mid-August: renewed IRGC-attributed drone attacks on two ADNOC tankers Aug 13 (0 injuries) followed the Aug 8 missile strike; separately, the Russian tanker Caroline Bezengi ran aground near al-Qibliyah Island off southern Oman on Aug 14, causing an oil leak (Oman TV). Iran and Oman had not reached a route agreement as of Aug 14; Iran (Rezaei/Baghaei/Araghchi) insists the strait stays shut until US conditions are met (blockade lifted, funds unfrozen).. Method: Asymmetric denial via drone and missile strikes on commercial vessels, triggering insurance-driven shutdown. IRGC used sea drones, anti-ship missiles, and shore-launched projectiles to strike 21+ vessels since Feb 28. War risk insurance withdrawn or repriced at ~5% of vessel value — a 100x increase from pre-war 0.02-0.05%. For a $100M tanker, $5M per transit. At least one tanker paid $2M for transit rights through Iran-approved Larak Island corridor. Trump ordered DFC to provide $20B in political risk reinsurance (Chubb as lead underwriter), but JPMorgan estimates actual exposure at $352B across 329 tankers. Reports of naval mine deployment began ~March 10; US destroyed 44+ Iranian minelayers. Iran's stockpile estimated at 2,000-6,000 naval mines. Iran retains 80%+ of its small boats and minelayers. London Joint War Committee extended high-risk area to include waters around Oman.

Drone swarm overwhelms air defenses at Al Udeid, Qatar: A coordinated salvo of 40+ Shahed drones and 5 ballistic missiles targets Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar — the largest US air base in the Middle East. Most are intercepted but 3 drones penetrate defenses and strike the airfield, damaging a KC-135 tanker aircraft. No US fatalities. The incident raises questions about interceptor stockpile sustainability.

strike_notes: DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8-14): renewed IRGC-claimed strikes on Ali Al Salem AB (and Camp Arifjan) Jul 8-13 after the ceasefire collapse — no US casualties; IRGC claims (2 HIMARS destroyed) unverified; see kuwait-ali-al-salem-arifjan for detail. PRIOR: Day 103 (June 10): the IRGC struck Ali Al Salem Air Base with drones (intercepted) in retaliation for the June 9 US strikes — part of the multi-front June 10 salvo on Bahrain, Kuwait and a NEW Jordan (Azraq) front (see iran-strikes-gulf-bases-20260610). 386th Air Expeditionary Wing hub. Kuwaiti air defenses intercepted initial ballistic missiles on Feb 28; debris fell on base. Satellite imagery confirmed damage to 12+ structures, aircraft shelters, and runway areas. Camp Canada (Canadian forces) bunkers also damaged. On March 2, Kuwaiti F/A-18 shot down 3 US F-15Es in friendly fire incident — all 6 crew ejected safely. Italian 51st Stormo personnel sheltered in bunkers.

event_description: Al Udeid Air Base, Qatar: Shahab-3 MRBM / cruise missiles — Two missiles reached base on March 1. Early warning radar targeted. No US casualties reported.
strike_notes: CENTCOM forward HQ. Qatar Defence Ministry said it thwarted attacks per pre-approved security plan. Two missiles reached base on March 1 per Qatar's official news agency. Long-range early warning radar in northern Qatar also targeted. Dozens of explosions heard in Doha from Patriot intercepts.

event_description: Al Dhafra Air Base, UAE: Ballistic missiles / cruise missiles / drones — 8 total killed (2 armed forces, 6 foreign nationals). 131+ injured across UAE.
strike_notes: Mar 22-24: UAE intercepted 8+ UAVs and 3+ ballistic missiles. Day 25 (Mar 24): Ballistic missile targeting Abu Dhabi intercepted; 1 Indian national suffered minor injuries from debris. Cumulative damage includes hits on Al Dhafra AB, Dubai International Airport, Palm Jumeirah, Burj Al Arab, Jebel Ali Port. 8 people killed (2 military, 6 foreign national civilians). Habshan gas facilities shut down.

event_description: NSA Bahrain / NAVCENT HQ: Cruise missiles / ballistic missiles / drones — 2 killed. Bapco Sitra refinery under force majeure since March 9.
strike_notes: DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8-14): renewed IRGC-claimed missile/drone strikes on NSA Bahrain / Juffair and Sheikh Isa AB Jul 8, 12 and 13 after the ceasefire collapse — no US casualties (CENTCOM); downed drones damaged Bahraini homes; see bahrain-nsa-juffair for detail. PRIOR: Day 103 (June 10): the IRGC struck the US Fifth Fleet HQ (NSA Bahrain) with drones (intercepted) in retaliation for the June 9 US strikes — part of the multi-front June 10 salvo on Bahrain, Kuwait and a NEW Jordan (Azraq) front (see iran-strikes-gulf-bases-20260610). US Fifth Fleet / NAVCENT HQ. Day 26 (Mar 25): Bahrain air raid sirens activated. Cumulative since war start: 153 missiles and 301 drones intercepted. IRGC fires 'precision-guided' missiles and drones at US-hosting bases in Bahrain.

event_description: Haifa, Israel: Hezbollah rockets and missiles / Iranian Kheibar Shekan MRBM (unverified) — Casualties reported but Haifa-specific figures unconfirmed. Major Israeli casualties were in Beit Shemesh (9 killed) and Tel Aviv, not Haifa.
weapon_system: Hezbollah rockets and missiles / Iranian Kheibar Shekan MRBM (unverified)
strike_notes: Hezbollah targeted missile defense site south of Haifa on March 2, first strikes since 2024 ceasefire. Hezbollah also launched drone swarm at Ramat David airbase targeting radar sites and control rooms. Direct Iranian missile fire at Haifa unverified — most Haifa-area attacks attributed to Hezbollah.

event_description: Tel Aviv, Israel: Fattah hypersonic / cruise missiles / cluster munitions — 18 Israeli civilians killed total since Feb 28. 4,002+ injured. Thai worker killed by cluster munitions at Adanim (Mar 19). 3 women killed in West Bank salon (Mar 19).
weapon_system: Fattah hypersonic / cruise missiles / cluster munitions
strike_notes: Day 26 (Mar 25): Missile hits Tel Aviv street — air defenses fail to intercept. Significant property damage, vehicles destroyed. Missile alerts across Israel: sirens in Dimona (near Negev Nuclear Research Center), Eilat, Netanya, central Israel. IRGC fires 'precision-guided' missiles and drones at Israel. Total Israeli killed since Feb 28: 17-18 (15 civilians + 2-3 soldiers). 4,800+ wounded (Al Jazeera tracker).

event_description: Beirut / Southern Suburbs: Israeli airstrikes (in response to Hezbollah entry) — 1,001+ killed including 118+ children. 2,584+ wounded. 1M+ displaced (~1/5 of population).
weapon_system: Israeli airstrikes (in response to Hezbollah entry)
strike_notes: Hezbollah entered war March 2 after Khamenei assassination. IDF struck 2,000+ targets in Lebanon since March 2, eliminating 570+ operatives including 220 Radwan Force members. Hassan Ali Marwan (new Imam Hussein Division commander) eliminated Mar 19 — predecessor killed prior week. Ahmad Abdallah (Hamas military wing commander) died of wounds from Mar 11 strike in Beirut. Hezbollah: 668 cumulative attack waves on Israel (daily avg 37, trending up). 54 attack waves on Mar 19 — among highest single-day totals. IDF issued widespread evacuation orders in southern Lebanon Mar 20. 1M+ displaced — UNHCR warns families struggling to find shelter.

event_description: Tyre, Lebanon: Israeli airstrikes — Included in Lebanese total
strike_notes: Southern Lebanese city, Hezbollah rocket launch sites targeted. IDF issued evacuation orders for all residents south of Litani on ~Day 5, affecting 250-300 settlements. IDF 36th Division operating in southern Lebanon as of March 9. Limited incursions and active combat between IDF and Hezbollah confirmed in eastern sector near Khiyam and Ed Dhayra. Large-scale invasion south of Litani being planned but NOT YET LAUNCHED as of March 13.

event_description: Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia: Cruise missiles / drones (Houthi) — Infrastructure damage — no casualties reported
strike_notes: World's largest oil loading facility. Saudi Arabia confirmed shooting down two drones, debris started limited fire. No civilian injuries. Saudi Aramco warned of 'catastrophic consequences' for oil markets. Saudi Arabia increasingly diverted oil to Red Sea port of Yanbu via East-West Crude Oil Pipeline.

event_description: Strait of Hormuz (maritime): Anti-ship missiles / drones / naval mines / explosive unmanned surface vessels / coastal batteries — 47+ ships/tugs/rigs hit or near a strike site since Feb 28 (IMO cumulative; +1 with the June 25 Ever Lovely strike); 11 seafarer fatalities to date. Earlier March breakdown: 8 bulk carriers (40%), 6 tankers (30%), 4 container ships (20%), 2 service vessels (10%) attacked.
weapon_system: Anti-ship missiles / drones / naval mines / explosive unmanned surface vessels / coastal batteries
strike_notes: UKMTO: 20+ confirmed maritime security incidents since Feb 28. Two additional vessels struck Mar 20. Only 21 tankers have crossed the Strait since Feb 28 vs 100+/day pre-war. Half of March transits by shadow fleet (Lloyd's List). Iran selectively allowing passage: India (2 LPG tankers), Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi each transited with individual approval. War risk premiums: 0.125% to ~5% of vessel value (40x increase). $5M per transit for $100M tanker. VLCC rates hit all-time record $423,736/day. GPS/AIS disruption: 44 injected signal zones, 92 denial areas. IMO emergency session Mar 18-19: negotiating safe maritime corridor for seafarer evacuation. UPDATE (June 7): IMO cumulative now 46+ ships/tugs/rigs hit or near a strike site since Feb 28, with 11 seafarer deaths to date; most recently the containership MSC Sariska V was damaged by a drone June 1 at Umm Qasr, Iraq (Manifest §3b). UPDATE (June 25): after the June 17-18 toll-free reopening, the IRGC reasserted permission-only Hormuz transit (VHF Ch.16 warnings) and struck the Singapore-flagged container ship Ever Lovely (bridge damaged, no casualties) ~7.5nm SE of Dahit, Oman — the first ship attack since the reopening (detail under 2026-06-25-hormuz-ever-lovely); 3 tankers turned back and 3 diverted, and the UN IMO paused its plan to evacuate ~11,000 stranded seafarers. Iran is reportedly seeking ~$40B/yr in transit fees once the 60-day free-passage window lapses (WSJ). DAY 170 UPDATE (Aug 16): IRGC-attributed vessel attacks have continued into mid-August — a UAE/ADNOC tanker hit by missile Aug 8 and two ADNOC tankers drone-struck Aug 13 (0 injuries), plus renewed Houthi Red Sea targeting of Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery Aug 14. ADNOC reports ~15-17 of its vessels attacked since Feb 28 (running total disputed).

event_description: Camp Buehring, Kuwait: Drones — 1 US National Guard soldier died of health-related incident on March 6 (Maj. Sorffly Davius, 46, NYPD officer). Not classified as combat death.
strike_notes: Northeastern Kuwait. Iranian drone struck the US garrison. Maj. Davius died during medical emergency at Camp Buehring on March 6 — incident under investigation, classified as health-related, not combat. IRGC claimed 230-drone wave targeting Camp Buehring among other Kuwait facilities on Day 6.

event_description: US Embassy, Hawalli, Kuwait: Missile (type unconfirmed) — Unknown — embassy personnel sheltering in place
strike_notes: US Embassy in Kuwait likely hit by Iranian missile strike per Wikipedia citing multiple sources. Xinhua published screenshot showing smoke billowing near embassy area on March 2. US Embassy warned public not to approach, all personnel sheltering in place. US embassies in Saudi Arabia and UAE consulate in Dubai also reportedly targeted by drones during the week.

strike_notes: Day 25 (Mar 24): IRGC attacked US 5th Fleet HQ in Bahrain with missiles and drones. 1 Emirati soldier KIA alongside Bahraini forces — first confirmed UAE combat death in direct Iranian attack. Cumulative war total: 153 missiles and 301 drones intercepted.

event_description: UAE (nationwide): Ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, drones — Cumulative: 438 ballistic missiles, 2,012 drones, 19 cruise missiles absorbed. Abu Dhabi airport and Dubai landmarks struck.
strike_notes: Day 36 cumulative update: UAE has absorbed the heaviest bombardment of any GCC state — 438 ballistic missiles, 2,012 drones, and 19 cruise missiles as of April 1. Abu Dhabi airport struck. Dubai landmarks damaged. This entry tracks the cumulative Iranian campaign against the UAE.

event_description: Tehran: Leadership House compound (Feb 28, Day 1)
strike_notes: Continuous bombardment since Day 1. Supreme Leader Khamenei killed in initial strike on Leadership House compound along with his daughter, son-in-law, grandchild, and daughter-in-law Zahra Haddad-Adel. Defense Minister Aziz Nasirzadeh, IRGC commander Mohammad Pakpour, chief of staff Abdolrahim Mousavi, Ali Shamkhani, and multiple other senior officials also killed. Mojtaba Khamenei (son) injured but survived; named new Supreme Leader on Mar 8 (Day 9). Day 11 (Mar 10): 40+ killed in Resalat Square residential area strike in eastern Tehran (see tehran-east-residential). Day 12: IDF destroys IRGC Air Force HQ (see tehran-irgc-af-hq). 460+ killed and 4,300+ wounded in Tehran alone as of Day 11 per Tehran Emergency Health Department. Days 20-21: Ali Mohammad Naini (IRGC spokesperson) killed in IAF airstrike overnight Mar 19-20. Day 22: Continued strikes on Tehran military and government infrastructure. Day 24 (Mar 23): IDF launched 'broad wave of attacks' on Tehran. Day 25 (Mar 24): IAF struck 50+ targets overnight. Day 26 (Mar 25): IDF launches 'new wide-scale attacks' on Iranian government infrastructure, including Tehran targets. South Tehran strike kills at least 12, wounds 28. Eastern Tehran strikes destroy school and residential buildings. Day 33 (Apr 1): Airstrike hit former US Embassy compound on Taleghani Street — IRGC-controlled since 1979 — internally detonating penetrator. Russian embassy across the street confirmed blast broke doors/windows at St. Nicholas Orthodox Cathedral and partially collapsed adjacent Russian nursing home.

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: Strait of Hormuz (maritime): Anti-ship missiles / drones / naval mines / explosive unmanned surface vessels / coastal batteries — 47+ ships/tugs/rigs hit or near a strike site since Feb 28 (IMO cumulative; +1 with the June 25 Ever Lovely strike); 11 seafarer fatalities to date. weapon_system: Anti-ship missiles / drones / naval mines / explosive unmanned surface vessels / coastal batteries
strike_notes: UKMTO: 20+ confirmed maritime security incidents since Feb 28. Two additional vessels struck Mar 20. Only 21 tankers have crossed the Strait since Feb 28 vs 100+/day pre-war. Half of March transits by shadow fleet (Lloyd's List). Iran selectively allowing passage: India (2 LPG tankers), Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi each transited with individual approval. War risk premiums: 0.125% to ~5% of vessel value (40x increase). $5M per transit for $100M tanker. VLCC rates hit all-time record $423,736/day. GPS/AIS disruption: 44 injected signal zones, 92 denial areas. IMO emergency session Mar 18-19: negotiating safe maritime corridor for seafarer evacuation. UPDATE (June 7): IMO cumulative now 46+ ships/tugs/rigs hit or near a strike site since Feb 28, with 11 seafarer deaths to date; most recently the containership MSC Sariska V was damaged by a drone June 1 at Umm Qasr, Iraq (Manifest §3b). UPDATE (June 25): after the June 17-18 toll-free reopening, the IRGC reasserted permission-only Hormuz transit (VHF Ch.16 warnings) and struck the Singapore-flagged container ship Ever Lovely (bridge damaged, no casualties) ~7.5nm SE of Dahit, Oman — the first ship attack since the reopening (detail under 2026-06-25-hormuz-ever-lovely); 3 tankers turned back and 3 diverted, and the UN IMO paused its plan to evacuate ~11,000 stranded seafarers. Iran is reportedly seeking ~$40B/yr in transit fees once the 60-day free-passage window lapses (WSJ). DAY 170 UPDATE (Aug 16): IRGC-attributed vessel attacks have continued into mid-August — a UAE/ADNOC tanker hit by missile Aug 8 and two ADNOC tankers drone-struck Aug 13 (0 injuries), plus renewed Houthi Red Sea targeting of Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery Aug 14. Defense Minister Aziz Nasirzadeh, IRGC commander Mohammad Pakpour, chief of staff Abdolrahim Mousavi, Ali Shamkhani, and multiple other senior officials also killed. Mojtaba Khamenei (son) injured but survived; named new Supreme Leader on Mar 8 (Day 9). Day 11 (Mar 10): 40+ killed in Resalat Square residential area strike in eastern Tehran (see tehran-east-residential). Day 12: IDF destroys IRGC Air Force HQ (see tehran-irgc-af-hq). 460+ killed and 4,300+ wounded in Tehran alone as of Day 11 per Tehran Emergency Health Department. Days 20-21: Ali Mohammad Naini (IRGC spokesperson) killed in IAF airstrike overnight Mar 19-20. Day 22: Continued strikes on Tehran military and government infrastructure. Day 24 (Mar 23): IDF launched 'broad wave of attacks' on Tehran. Day 25 (Mar 24): IAF struck 50+ targets overnight. Day 26 (Mar 25): IDF launches 'new wide-scale attacks' on Iranian government infrastructure, including Tehran targets. South Tehran strike kills at least 12, wounds 28. Eastern Tehran strikes destroy school and residential buildings. Day 33 (Apr 1): Airstrike hit former US Embassy compound on Taleghani Street — IRGC-controlled since 1979 — internally detonating penetrator. Russian embassy across the street confirmed blast broke doors/windows at St. Nicholas Orthodox Cathedral and partially collapsed adjacent Russian nursing home.

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: Kharg Island: Oil export terminal
strike_notes: 90% of Iran's oil exports flow through Kharg. Struck in second-week escalation. Israel bombed 30 additional oil depots on Day 10. Day 15 (Mar 13): US executed large-scale precision strike on 90+ military targets including naval mine storage, missile storage bunkers, air defense facility, naval base, airport control tower/runway, and helicopter hangar. Oil infrastructure deliberately preserved. Trump warned of future strikes if Hormuz remains blocked. Trump called it 'one of the most powerful bombing raids in the History of the Middle East.' Day 16: Trump threatens to hit Kharg again 'just for fun.' | Addendum: Day 72 (May 10) NYT/ANI report cites Orbital EOS estimating spill expanded to >20 sq mi by Thursday (~3,000 bbl released); BusinessToday cites 80,000 bbl over 27 sq mi cumulative since May 5. Conflict and Environment Observatory says slick 'much reduced' on May 9 Sentinel imagery vs ~45 sq km peak. Iranian denials reiterated (MP Pourkabgani; energy commission chief Moussa Ahmadi). Cause UNVERIFIED — could be (a) US blockade-induced overflow of storage at 74%→80% capacity threshold, (b) deliberate Iranian discharge, (c) Western-tanker ballast dump per Iranian counter-narrative.

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: Kharg Island: Oil export terminal
strike_notes: 90% of Iran's oil exports flow through Kharg. Struck in second-week escalation. Israel bombed 30 additional oil depots on Day 10. Day 15 (Mar 13): US executed large-scale precision strike on 90+ military targets including naval mine storage, missile storage bunkers, air defense facility, naval base, airport control tower/runway, and helicopter hangar. Oil infrastructure deliberately preserved. Trump warned of future strikes if Hormuz remains blocked. Trump called it 'one of the most powerful bombing raids in the History of the Middle East.' Day 16: Trump threatens to hit Kharg again 'just for fun.' | Addendum: Day 72 (May 10) NYT/ANI report cites Orbital EOS estimating spill expanded to >20 sq mi by Thursday (~3,000 bbl released); BusinessToday cites 80,000 bbl over 27 sq mi cumulative since May 5. Conflict and Environment Observatory says slick 'much reduced' on May 9 Sentinel imagery vs ~45 sq km peak. Iranian denials reiterated (MP Pourkabgani; energy commission chief Moussa Ahmadi). Cause UNVERIFIED — could be (a) US blockade-induced overflow of storage at 74%→80% capacity threshold, (b) deliberate Iranian discharge, (c) Western-tanker ballast dump per Iranian counter-narrative.

Inspectors were evacuated before the strikes. Iran announced withdrawal from the NPT on March 2. IAEA states it 'cannot assess the current status of Iran's nuclear material inventory.' The war intended to prevent an Iranian bomb may have made verification of that goal impossible.

event_description: Strait of Hormuz (maritime): Anti-ship missiles / drones / naval mines / explosive unmanned surface vessels / coastal batteries — 47+ ships/tugs/rigs hit or near a strike site since Feb 28 (IMO cumulative; +1 with the June 25 Ever Lovely strike); 11 seafarer fatalities to date. Earlier March breakdown: 8 bulk carriers (40%), 6 tankers (30%), 4 container ships (20%), 2 service vessels (10%) attacked.

strike_notes: UKMTO: 20+ confirmed maritime security incidents since Feb 28. Two additional vessels struck Mar 20. Only 21 tankers have crossed the Strait since Feb 28 vs 100+/day pre-war. Half of March transits by shadow fleet (Lloyd's List). Iran selectively allowing passage: India (2 LPG tankers), Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi each transited with individual approval. UPDATE (June 7): IMO cumulative now 46+ ships/tugs/rigs hit or near a strike site since Feb 28, with 11 seafarer deaths to date; most recently the containership MSC Sariska V was damaged by a drone June 1 at Umm Qasr, Iraq (Manifest §3b). UPDATE (June 25): after the June 17-18 toll-free reopening, the IRGC reasserted permission-only Hormuz transit (VHF Ch.16 warnings) and struck the Singapore-flagged container ship Ever Lovely (bridge damaged, no casualties) ~7.5nm SE of Dahit, Oman — the first ship attack since the reopening (detail under 2026-06-25-hormuz-ever-lovely); 3 tankers turned back and 3 diverted, and the UN IMO paused its plan to evacuate ~11,000 stranded seafarers. Iran is reportedly seeking ~$40B/yr in transit fees once the 60-day free-passage window lapses (WSJ). DAY 170 UPDATE (Aug 16): IRGC-attributed vessel attacks have continued into mid-August — a UAE/ADNOC tanker hit by missile Aug 8 and two ADNOC tankers drone-struck Aug 13 (0 injuries), plus renewed Houthi Red Sea targeting of Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery Aug 14. ADNOC reports ~15-17 of its vessels attacked since Feb 28 (running total disputed).

event_description: Tehran: Leadership House compound (Feb 28, Day 1)
strike_notes: Continuous bombardment since Day 1. Supreme Leader Khamenei killed in initial strike on Leadership House compound along with his daughter, son-in-law, grandchild, and daughter-in-law Zahra Haddad-Adel. Defense Minister Aziz Nasirzadeh, IRGC commander Mohammad Pakpour, chief of staff Abdolrahim Mousavi, Ali Shamkhani, and multiple other senior officials also killed. Mojtaba Khamenei (son) injured but survived; named new Supreme Leader on Mar 8 (Day 9). Day 11 (Mar 10): 40+ killed in Resalat Square residential area strike in eastern Tehran (see tehran-east-residential). Day 12: IDF destroys IRGC Air Force HQ (see tehran-irgc-af-hq). 460+ killed and 4,300+ wounded in Tehran alone as of Day 11 per Tehran Emergency Health Department. Days 20-21: Ali Mohammad Naini (IRGC spokesperson) killed in IAF airstrike overnight Mar 19-20. Day 22: Continued strikes on Tehran military and government infrastructure. Day 24 (Mar 23): IDF launched 'broad wave of attacks' on Tehran. Day 25 (Mar 24): IAF struck 50+ targets overnight. Day 26 (Mar 25): IDF launches 'new wide-scale attacks' on Iranian government infrastructure, including Tehran targets. South Tehran strike kills at least 12, wounds 28. Eastern Tehran strikes destroy school and residential buildings. Day 33 (Apr 1): Airstrike hit former US Embassy compound on Taleghani Street — IRGC-controlled since 1979 — internally detonating penetrator. Russian embassy across the street confirmed blast broke doors/windows at St. Nicholas Orthodox Cathedral and partially collapsed adjacent Russian nursing home.

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: Kharg Island: Oil export terminal
strike_notes: 90% of Iran's oil exports flow through Kharg. Struck in second-week escalation. Israel bombed 30 additional oil depots on Day 10. Day 15 (Mar 13): US executed large-scale precision strike on 90+ military targets including naval mine storage, missile storage bunkers, air defense facility, naval base, airport control tower/runway, and helicopter hangar. Oil infrastructure deliberately preserved. Trump warned of future strikes if Hormuz remains blocked. Trump called it 'one of the most powerful bombing raids in the History of the Middle East.' Day 16: Trump threatens to hit Kharg again 'just for fun.' | Addendum: Day 72 (May 10) NYT/ANI report cites Orbital EOS estimating spill expanded to >20 sq mi by Thursday (~3,000 bbl released); BusinessToday cites 80,000 bbl over 27 sq mi cumulative since May 5. Conflict and Environment Observatory says slick 'much reduced' on May 9 Sentinel imagery vs ~45 sq km peak. Iranian denials reiterated (MP Pourkabgani; energy commission chief Moussa Ahmadi). Cause UNVERIFIED — could be (a) US blockade-induced overflow of storage at 74%→80% capacity threshold, (b) deliberate Iranian discharge, (c) Western-tanker ballast dump per Iranian counter-narrative.

event_description: Trump sends mixed signals on war's end: President Trump tells CBS News the war is 'pretty much complete' but later tells House Republicans 'we haven't won enough.' Demands 'unconditional surrender' from Iran. Mixed messaging roils markets and confuses diplomatic channels.

Oil crashes after Energy Secretary's false Hormuz claim: Energy Secretary Chris Wright posts on social media that the US Navy has escorted a tanker through the Strait of Hormuz. The claim is false — no escort occurred. Brent crude plunges 11.3% to $87.80 before partially recovering. The incident raises questions about information discipline within the administration during wartime.

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: Kharg Island: Oil export terminal
strike_notes: 90% of Iran's oil exports flow through Kharg. Struck in second-week escalation. Israel bombed 30 additional oil depots on Day 10. Day 15 (Mar 13): US executed large-scale precision strike on 90+ military targets including naval mine storage, missile storage bunkers, air defense facility, naval base, airport control tower/runway, and helicopter hangar. Oil infrastructure deliberately preserved. Trump warned of future strikes if Hormuz remains blocked. Trump called it 'one of the most powerful bombing raids in the History of the Middle East.' Day 16: Trump threatens to hit Kharg again 'just for fun.' | Addendum: Day 72 (May 10) NYT/ANI report cites Orbital EOS estimating spill expanded to >20 sq mi by Thursday (~3,000 bbl released); BusinessToday cites 80,000 bbl over 27 sq mi cumulative since May 5. Cause UNVERIFIED — could be (a) US blockade-induced overflow of storage at 74%→80% capacity threshold, (b) deliberate Iranian discharge, (c) Western-tanker ballast dump per Iranian counter-narrative.
