event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: Kharg Island: Oil export terminal
strike_notes: 90% of Iran's oil exports flow through Kharg. Struck in second-week escalation. Israel bombed 30 additional oil depots on Day 10. Day 15 (Mar 13): US executed large-scale precision strike on 90+ military targets including naval mine storage, missile storage bunkers, air defense facility, naval base, airport control tower/runway, and helicopter hangar. Oil infrastructure deliberately preserved. Trump warned of future strikes if Hormuz remains blocked. Trump called it 'one of the most powerful bombing raids in the History of the Middle East.' Day 16: Trump threatens to hit Kharg again 'just for fun.' | Addendum: Day 72 (May 10) NYT/ANI report cites Orbital EOS estimating spill expanded to >20 sq mi by Thursday (~3,000 bbl released); BusinessToday cites 80,000 bbl over 27 sq mi cumulative since May 5. Conflict and Environment Observatory says slick 'much reduced' on May 9 Sentinel imagery vs ~45 sq km peak. Iranian denials reiterated (MP Pourkabgani; energy commission chief Moussa Ahmadi). Cause UNVERIFIED — could be (a) US blockade-induced overflow of storage at 74%→80% capacity threshold, (b) deliberate Iranian discharge, (c) Western-tanker ballast dump per Iranian counter-narrative.

event_description: Senate begins heated AUMF debate: The US Senate takes up the Authorization for Use of Military Force resolution demanded by 34 senators. Floor debate is heated — supporters argue the war is unconstitutional without explicit Congressional authorization; opponents call the debate 'aiding the enemy during wartime.' White House issues statement reaffirming Article II authority. Vote expected within 24 hours. Markets watch closely — an AUMF rejection could force a withdrawal timeline.
timeline_data_point: AUMF floor debate begins — vote expected March 14

event_description: Russia introduces rival ceasefire resolution at UNSC: Russia introduces its own ceasefire resolution at the UN Security Council, calling for an immediate cessation of hostilities, withdrawal of all foreign forces from Iranian territory, and an international conference on Persian Gulf security. Unlike China's vetoed resolution, Russia's draft includes language condemning 'unilateral military aggression.' US, UK, and France expected to veto. Diplomatic paralysis at the UNSC deepens.
timeline_data_point: Second ceasefire resolution in 48 hours — US veto expected

event_description: EU announces sanctions package on IRGC and Iranian oil: The European Union announces a comprehensive sanctions package targeting IRGC leadership, Iranian oil exports, and entities supporting Iran's ballistic missile program. The EU simultaneously calls for an 'immediate humanitarian pause' and offers to mediate. Iran responds by recalling its ambassadors from France, Germany, and the Netherlands. The sanctions signal Europe is aligning with the US position while maintaining diplomatic distance.
timeline_data_point: EU sanctions on IRGC + Iranian oil — Iran recalls 3 ambassadors

WTI holds flat at $95.28. Analysts caution that the psychological impact of convoys exceeds the material impact — 5 tankers cannot replace 50. The fundamental shortfall of 12.35 MBD persists. Gold eases to $5,080/oz.

S&P 500 closes at 6,672.62 — slight decline on continued uncertainty: Markets drift lower as the AUMF debate introduces political uncertainty. S&P 500 closes at 6,672.62, down 0.3% on the day and 3.0% below pre-war levels. Defense stocks remain elevated at +16.5%. Oil majors ease 1% with crude. Airlines extend losses to -24.5% as fuel cost fears mount. VIX holds at 27.5 — elevated but below crisis peaks.

Gas prices hit $3.82/gallon — trucking surcharges take effect: National average gas price climbs to $3.82/gallon — up 28.2% from pre-war $2.98. California hits $5.15/gallon. The trucking industry's war surcharges announced yesterday take effect today, adding 8-12% to freight costs. Grocery chains warn of price increases on perishables within 3-5 days. The war's cost is no longer abstract — it is arriving at every checkout counter in America.
timeline_source: AAA / GasBuddy / American Trucking Associations / YCharts
timeline_data_point: $3.82/gal — +28.2% since pre-war. CA at $5.15

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: Kharg Island: Oil export terminal
strike_notes: 90% of Iran's oil exports flow through Kharg. Struck in second-week escalation. Israel bombed 30 additional oil depots on Day 10. Day 15 (Mar 13): US executed large-scale precision strike on 90+ military targets including naval mine storage, missile storage bunkers, air defense facility, naval base, airport control tower/runway, and helicopter hangar. Oil infrastructure deliberately preserved. Trump warned of future strikes if Hormuz remains blocked. Trump called it 'one of the most powerful bombing raids in the History of the Middle East.' Day 16: Trump threatens to hit Kharg again 'just for fun.' | Addendum: Day 72 (May 10) NYT/ANI report cites Orbital EOS estimating spill expanded to >20 sq mi by Thursday (~3,000 bbl released); BusinessToday cites 80,000 bbl over 27 sq mi cumulative since May 5. Conflict and Environment Observatory says slick 'much reduced' on May 9 Sentinel imagery vs ~45 sq km peak. Iranian denials reiterated (MP Pourkabgani; energy commission chief Moussa Ahmadi). Cause UNVERIFIED — could be (a) US blockade-induced overflow of storage at 74%→80% capacity threshold, (b) deliberate Iranian discharge, (c) Western-tanker ballast dump per Iranian counter-narrative.

strike_notes: UKMTO: 20+ confirmed maritime security incidents since Feb 28. Two additional vessels struck Mar 20. Only 21 tankers have crossed the Strait since Feb 28 vs 100+/day pre-war. Half of March transits by shadow fleet (Lloyd's List). Iran selectively allowing passage: India (2 LPG tankers), Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi each transited with individual approval. War risk premiums: 0.125% to ~5% of vessel value (40x increase). $5M per transit for $100M tanker. VLCC rates hit all-time record $423,736/day. GPS/AIS disruption: 44 injected signal zones, 92 denial areas. IMO emergency session Mar 18-19: negotiating safe maritime corridor for seafarer evacuation. UPDATE (June 7): IMO cumulative now 46+ ships/tugs/rigs hit or near a strike site since Feb 28, with 11 seafarer deaths to date; most recently the containership MSC Sariska V was damaged by a drone June 1 at Umm Qasr, Iraq (Manifest §3b). UPDATE (June 25): after the June 17-18 toll-free reopening, the IRGC reasserted permission-only Hormuz transit (VHF Ch.16 warnings) and struck the Singapore-flagged container ship Ever Lovely (bridge damaged, no casualties) ~7.5nm SE of Dahit, Oman — the first ship attack since the reopening (detail under 2026-06-25-hormuz-ever-lovely); 3 tankers turned back and 3 diverted, and the UN IMO paused its plan to evacuate ~11,000 stranded seafarers. Iran is reportedly seeking ~$40B/yr in transit fees once the 60-day free-passage window lapses (WSJ). DAY 170 UPDATE (Aug 16): IRGC-attributed vessel attacks have continued into mid-August — a UAE/ADNOC tanker hit by missile Aug 8 and two ADNOC tankers drone-struck Aug 13 (0 injuries), plus renewed Houthi Red Sea targeting of Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery Aug 14. ADNOC reports ~15-17 of its vessels attacked since Feb 28 (running total disputed).

event_description: Fujairah Oil Hub, UAE: Drones — No casualties reported. Oil-loading operations suspended twice.
casualties_reported: No casualties reported. Oil-loading operations suspended twice.
strike_notes: Key strategic target — Fujairah is the terminus of the UAE's Habshan-Fujairah pipeline (1.5 mbd capacity), the primary bypass route for oil exports around the Strait of Hormuz. First attack March 14: intercepted drone debris struck bunkering facility, starting fire and suspending oil-loading. Second attack March 16: direct drone strike, oil-loading suspended again. Two shutdowns in three days signals deliberate Iranian strategy to close the Hormuz bypass. If Fujairah stays offline, the 12.35 mbd shortfall widens to 13.85 mbd.

Supreme Leader Khamenei killed in initial strike on Leadership House compound along with his daughter, son-in-law, grandchild, and daughter-in-law Zahra Haddad-Adel. Defense Minister Aziz Nasirzadeh, IRGC commander Mohammad Pakpour, chief of staff Abdolrahim Mousavi, Ali Shamkhani, and multiple other senior officials also killed. event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: Australia and Japan refuse to send warships to Hormuz: Despite President Trump's public call for allied nations to deploy warships to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz, both Australia and Japan decline. Australia's Defense Minister says the commitment is 'not appropriate at this time.' Japan's PM rules out sending naval assets. No allied nation has made a firm commitment to join US escort operations, underscoring the diplomatic isolation of the US-led war effort.
timeline_data_point: Australia and Japan refuse Hormuz warship request

event_description: Iran FM: 'We never asked for a ceasefire' — diplomacy stalls: Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi declares 'We never asked for a ceasefire' and vows Iran 'is ready to defend ourselves as long as it takes.' The Trump administration separately rebuffs ceasefire efforts by Middle Eastern allies. Oman's mediation attempt fails to produce talks. The Pope calls for an immediate ceasefire. China condemns the attacks. A US Senate vote to curb Trump's war powers fails 47-53.
timeline_data_point: Both sides reject ceasefire — Senate AUMF vote fails 47-53

event_description: 56% of Americans oppose the war — NPR/PBS/Marist poll: A new NPR/PBS NewsHour/Marist poll finds 56% of Americans are against the war with Iran. The figure represents a significant public opinion shift given that the conflict is only 17 days old. Combined with the failed Senate AUMF vote (47-53) and the approaching $50B supplemental request, domestic political pressure on the war effort is building.
timeline_data_point: 56% opposed — first majority-oppose poll of the war

Half of March transits by shadow fleet (Lloyd's List). Iran selectively allowing passage: India (2 LPG tankers), Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi each transited with individual approval. War risk premiums: 0.125% to ~5% of vessel value (40x increase). $5M per transit for $100M tanker. VLCC rates hit all-time record $423,736/day. GPS/AIS disruption: 44 injected signal zones, 92 denial areas. IMO emergency session Mar 18-19: negotiating safe maritime corridor for seafarer evacuation. UPDATE (June 7): IMO cumulative now 46+ ships/tugs/rigs hit or near a strike site since Feb 28, with 11 seafarer deaths to date; most recently the containership MSC Sariska V was damaged by a drone June 1 at Umm Qasr, Iraq (Manifest §3b). UPDATE (June 25): after the June 17-18 toll-free reopening, the IRGC reasserted permission-only Hormuz transit (VHF Ch.16 warnings) and struck the Singapore-flagged container ship Ever Lovely (bridge damaged, no casualties) ~7.5nm SE of Dahit, Oman — the first ship attack since the reopening (detail under 2026-06-25-hormuz-ever-lovely); 3 tankers turned back and 3 diverted, and the UN IMO paused its plan to evacuate ~11,000 stranded seafarers. Iran is reportedly seeking ~$40B/yr in transit fees once the 60-day free-passage window lapses (WSJ). DAY 170 UPDATE (Aug 16): IRGC-attributed vessel attacks have continued into mid-August — a UAE/ADNOC tanker hit by missile Aug 8 and two ADNOC tankers drone-struck Aug 13 (0 injuries), plus renewed Houthi Red Sea targeting of Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery Aug 14. ADNOC reports ~15-17 of its vessels attacked since Feb 28 (running total disputed).

event_description: Fujairah Oil Hub, UAE: Drones — No casualties reported. Oil-loading operations suspended twice.
strike_notes: Key strategic target — Fujairah is the terminus of the UAE's Habshan-Fujairah pipeline (1.5 mbd capacity), the primary bypass route for oil exports around the Strait of Hormuz. First attack March 14: intercepted drone debris struck bunkering facility, starting fire and suspending oil-loading. Second attack March 16: direct drone strike, oil-loading suspended again. Two shutdowns in three days signals deliberate Iranian strategy to close the Hormuz bypass. If Fujairah stays offline, the 12.35 mbd shortfall widens to 13.85 mbd.

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: South Pars / Asaluyeh (Bushehr Province): South Pars natural gas field — Phases 3, 4, 5, 6
strike_notes: CRITICAL ESCALATION — First strike on Iran's upstream energy infrastructure since Operation Epic Fury began. Israeli Air Force with explicit US coordination struck South Pars Phases 3/4/5/6 and Asaluyeh hub early Wednesday March 18. Two refineries taken offline with combined capacity of ~100 million cubic meters/day of gas — roughly one-fifth of the field's total capacity. South Pars produces 730 million cm³ of gas/day, supplying 70% of Iran's domestic gas. Qatar immediately condemned the strike. Trump claimed US 'knew nothing' (sources contradicted). Netanyahu confirmed Mar 19 Israel would comply with Trump's demand to stop further energy strikes. IAEA DG Grossi told NPR enrichment capabilities will partially survive, contradicting Netanyahu. IRGC issued 'urgent warning' naming SAMREF, Jubail, Al Hosn, Mesaieed, Ras Laffan as retaliatory targets. Brent spiked to $119.11 intraday; TTF gas +30-33%.

weapon_system: Anti-ship missiles / drones / naval mines / explosive unmanned surface vessels / coastal batteries

Half of March transits by shadow fleet (Lloyd's List). Iran selectively allowing passage: India (2 LPG tankers), Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi each transited with individual approval. GPS/AIS disruption: 44 injected signal zones, 92 denial areas. IMO emergency session Mar 18-19: negotiating safe maritime corridor for seafarer evacuation. UPDATE (June 7): IMO cumulative now 46+ ships/tugs/rigs hit or near a strike site since Feb 28, with 11 seafarer deaths to date; most recently the containership MSC Sariska V was damaged by a drone June 1 at Umm Qasr, Iraq (Manifest §3b). UPDATE (June 25): after the June 17-18 toll-free reopening, the IRGC reasserted permission-only Hormuz transit (VHF Ch.16 warnings) and struck the Singapore-flagged container ship Ever Lovely (bridge damaged, no casualties) ~7.5nm SE of Dahit, Oman — the first ship attack since the reopening (detail under 2026-06-25-hormuz-ever-lovely); 3 tankers turned back and 3 diverted, and the UN IMO paused its plan to evacuate ~11,000 stranded seafarers. event_description: Ras Laffan Industrial City, Qatar: Ballistic missiles — Extensive damage. LNG Trains 4 and 6 damaged (12.8 MTPA = 17% of Qatar's LNG exports). Pearl GTL offline.

QatarEnergy confirmed LNG Trains 4 and 6 damaged — 12.8 MTPA, representing 17% of Qatar's LNG exports. Repair timeline: 3-5 years. Force majeure declared on contracts to Belgium, Italy, South Korea, China. Estimated revenue loss: ~$20B/year (~9% of Qatar's GDP). Pearl GTL (Shell-operated) also damaged — offline minimum 1 year. Qatar expelled Iran's military and security attachés within 24 hours. Wood Mackenzie: 'fundamentally reshaping the global LNG outlook.' TTF gas surged ~30-33%.

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: Natanz nuclear facility struck — IAEA confirms no radiation increase: The Natanz nuclear enrichment facility — Iran's primary uranium enrichment site — was struck on March 21. Iran's Mizan News confirmed the attack but claimed no radiation leakage. IAEA DG Rafael Grossi reported no increase in off-site radiation and called for 'military restraint to avoid any risk of a nuclear accident.' Israel denied responsibility; Iran blamed a joint US-Israeli strike. Russia condemned as posing 'real risk of catastrophic disaster.' This is the second Natanz strike during Operation Epic Fury and the third since June 2025 Operation Midnight Hammer.

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: IEA April OMR: Largest oil supply disruption in history — 10.1 mb/d March loss: The International Energy Agency released its April Oil Market Report, confirming the LARGEST OIL SUPPLY DISRUPTION IN HISTORY. Global supply fell 10.1 mb/d in March to 97 mb/d. Hormuz throughput collapsed to 3.8 mb/d (from >20 mb/d pre-war — an 80%+ decline). Cumulative supply losses exceed 360 million barrels in March with 440 million projected for April. Russia's oil revenues nearly doubled to $19B in March as buyers scrambled for alternatives to Gulf crude. The IEA now projects global oil demand will DECLINE 80,000 b/d in 2026 versus a prior forecast of +730,000 b/d growth — a swing of 810,000 b/d. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright stated prices will remain elevated until 'meaningful ship traffic' returns to Hormuz.

Blockade's first full day — only 3 vessels transit Hormuz, none to Iranian ports: The US naval blockade completed its first full day of operations. Only 3 commercial vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz — none of them bound for Iranian ports, meaning the blockade was NOT directly tested. The three ships: Rich Starry (Chinese-owned, Malawi-flagged, US-sanctioned, carrying 250,000 barrels of methanol — initially turned back near Qeshm Island before passing overnight); Murlikishan (US-sanctioned, has carried Russian/Iranian oil); and Peace Gulf (Panama-flagged, heading to UAE via an IRGC-ordered route). Pre-war ~140 ships/day. 600-800 vessels remain stranded in the Gulf, including 325 tankers and ~147 containerships (~470K TEU). An estimated 20,000 seafarers are trapped on ships. Dark vessel activity remains elevated: 3 non-AIS tankers observed berthing at Iranian ports, 14 non-AIS vessels in port waiting areas. CENTCOM established new routing to be shared with the maritime industry. Mine clearance continues via USS Pioneer and USS Chief dispatched from Singapore. Blockade estimated to cost Iran ~$435M/day (FDD).

CENTCOM 48-hour blockade update: 9 vessels turned back, no breaches: CENTCOM's 48-hour blockade update: 9 commercial vessels turned back with no successful Iranian-port breaches claimed. The first 24 hours saw 6 vessels turned back (Apr 14 daily figure from CENTCOM), climbing to 9 total by Apr 15. Adm. Brad Cooper stated the blockade is 'fully implemented' and Iran's sea trade is 'completely halted.' 10,000+ sailors, Marines, and airmen deployed; 12+ warships including USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72), USS Tripoli (LHA-7), and multiple guided-missile destroyers. Mine countermeasure operations ongoing. Specific interdictions: WSJ reports US forces intercepted 8 oil tankers entering/leaving Iranian ports; Reuters reports a US Navy destroyer interdicted 2 oil tankers leaving Chabahar port via radio warning; Kpler data shows vessel Ostria turned back before loading at Iranian port. 20+ non-Iran-bound commercial ships passed through the Strait freely per WSJ. Ambiguous transits: Rich Starry (Chinese-owned, sanctioned, false Malawian flag) exited Iran's outbound lane Apr 14, then reversed course into Gulf of Oman; Elpis (sanctioned) stopped at same point, then turned off transponder; 5 laden product tankers exited Iran's corridor around blockade start, now holding stationary in Gulf of Oman (Kpler). Iran's Tasnim claims commercial vessels 'set sail' despite blockade; CENTCOM denies breaches. CENTCOM's position is that vessels heading to non-Iranian ports are permitted — creating a definitional gap with Trump's original 'blockade ANY and all' formulation.

event_description: House REJECTS H.Con.Res.38 War Powers Resolution 213-214 — ONE VOTE margin: The House rejected H.Con.Res.38 War Powers Resolution 213-214 on Apr 16 — Congress came within one vote of halting the war. Rep. Thomas Massie was the only Republican in favor; Rep. Jared Golden was the only Democrat opposed; Rep. Warren Davidson voted present. Three Democrats (Vargas, Landsman, Cuellar) switched to support versus the March tally. The Senate rejected a War Powers Resolution 47-52 the prior day (Apr 15) — Rand Paul the lone Republican yes, Fetterman the lone Democratic no. The 60-day War Powers clock legally expires around May 1. With the House now also at single-digit margins, the next inflection will come with the appropriations/supplemental debate. Pentagon's $200B supplemental remains pending.

event_description: Iran rejects new face-to-face talks — Khatibzadeh: HEU transfer 'a non-starter': Iran rejected new face-to-face talks as currently constituted. Deputy FM Saeed Khatibzadeh, in Antalya, told AP that 'Americans are risking the international community, risking the global economy' and that Iran is 'not ready' for renewed direct talks because the US has 'not abandoned their maximalist position.' He confirmed Iran still holds 440 kg (970 lb) of enriched uranium and called the idea of transferring it out of the country 'a non-starter' — directly contradicting Trump's Friday claim that Tehran had agreed to do so. Pakistani FM Ishaq Dar, speaking from Antalya, said he expects to host a second round 'early next week' with Monday April 20 reported as feasible but not confirmed by the US side. Pakistani Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir spent April 18 in Tehran meeting senior Iranian officials; PM Shehbaz Sharif met with the Turkish president and Qatari emir in Antalya. Parliament security committee spokesman Ebrahim Rezaei announced drafted legislation replacing the informal $2M Hormuz tolls with a statutory 'strait security' charge. Iran's national security commission head Ebrahim Azizi confirmed the strait is 'returning to the status quo.'

event_description: Paris summit (Apr 17): 49 nations excl. US commit to Strait of Hormuz Freedom of Navigation Initiative: The Paris summit on April 17 at the Élysée — co-hosted by Macron and Starmer — convened 49 countries (many by video, including China, India, Canada, Australia, South Korea, Ukraine) for the Strait of Hormuz Maritime Freedom of Navigation Initiative. Macron: the mission will be 'a neutral mission, entirely separate from the belligerents.' Starmer: deployment 'as soon as conditions allow,' with roughly 12 countries pledging naval assets. Germany's Merz committed mine-clearance and maritime intelligence but conditioned participation on parliamentary approval and a UN Security Council legal basis, adding pointedly that Berlin would like US participation. Italy's Meloni offered Italian naval units. The US was conspicuously not invited to planning sessions, a remarkable rupture in transatlantic consultation. Polymarket odds of Hormuz returning to normal by end of April collapsed from 64% to roughly 32% on the April 18 re-closure news. IEA Director Fatih Birol warned April 16 that Europe has 'maybe six weeks or so of jet fuel left' if the strait remains disrupted, calling it the 'largest oil supply shock in history.'

HORMUZ RECLOSED — Iran Joint Military Command: control 'returned to its previous state': At roughly 05:19 ET, AP wires broke that Iran's Joint Military Command had announced via IRIB that 'control of the Strait of Hormuz has returned to its previous state … under strict management and control of the armed forces,' accusing the US of 'piracy and maritime robbery' for maintaining its port blockade after Iran declared the waterway open on Friday. Iranian Navy radio traffic monitored by Bloomberg and OSINT trackers instructed merchant vessels that no ships are allowed to pass through. Approximately 20 outbound tankers reversed course inside the strait (Kpler/TankerTrackers via WSJ). The reversal came hours after Trump declared 'no sticking points' remained in a deal. Parliament security committee spokesman Ebrahim Rezaei announced Iran is drafting legislation to replace the informal ~$2M-per-vessel toll with a statutory 'strait security' charge — US and Israeli military vessels barred entirely. National Security Commission head Ebrahim Azizi confirmed ships now require prior Iranian naval authorization.

event_description: Day 50 summary — Hormuz reclosed as ceasefire frays; Paris excludes US; markets face dangerous Monday gap: The April 18 reversal reveals the fundamental asymmetry of this ceasefire: the US holds overwhelming kinetic and blockade leverage, but Iran retains veto power over the strait at comparatively trivial cost. Trump's public claim of 'no sticking points' collides with Tehran's equally public refusal to surrender its 440 kg HEU stockpile — the original casus belli. Iran parliament announces draft 'Tehran Tollbooth' law — barring hostile country vessels: Iranian MP Mohammad-Reza Rezaei-Kouchi announced a parliamentary draft law that would codify the long-rumored 'Tehran Tollbooth' — barring 'hostile' country vessels from transiting the Strait of Hormuz and imposing statutory tolls on others. This represents a formal legislative response to Trump's Apr 13 blockade, replacing the informal ~$2M/vessel transit charge with codified legal architecture. Strait throughput is now >90% below pre-war baseline (~10 mb/d disrupted). UKMTO transit counts: 8 on Apr 9; 2 on Apr 10; 4 on Apr 11. War-risk insurance premiums surged from 0.125-0.2% to 0.5-1.0% of hull value per voyage ($1M per $100M tanker); Lloyd's Joint War Committee expanded its high-risk zone to cover the entire Persian Gulf. VLCC spot rates peaked at $423,736/day in March (LSEG record data). IEA April STEO: Brent peaks Q2 2026 at ~$115/bbl, falls below $90 Q4 2026, averages $76 in 2027.

event_description: Day 52 summary — ceasefire expires ~20:00 ET Tue Apr 21 after Touska seizure and Iran's rejection of Round 2 talks: As Day 52 of Operation Epic Fury closes, the two-week US-Iran ceasefire is ~24 hours from expiry and fraying in real time. Over Apr 17-20, Iran reopened then re-closed the Strait of Hormuz, USS Spruance seized the Iranian M/V Touska in the Gulf of Oman (Apr 19) in the first major kinetic enforcement of the blockade, Trump threatened to 'knock out every single Power Plant, and every single Bridge, in Iran,' and Iran's FM publicly signaled Tehran would not attend the Apr 20-21 Islamabad Round 2. Markets closed Friday on a ceasefire-hopes rally (S&P 500 +1.2% to 7,126 record) and reopened Monday sharply lower as oil surged 5-7%. The Islamabad delegation movement, Hormuz throughput, and the ceasefire expiry clock are the three variables now governing whether Day 53 is diplomacy or detonation. Cumulative direct US military expenditure ~$57.55B. Iran reporting frozen at pre-war levels due to a 50-day internet blackout (1,176 hours, longest ever recorded for a connected country); independent trackers have moved an order of magnitude higher (HRANA 3,636, Hengaw 6,620 military).

event_description: Day 54 summary — ceasefire indefinite, Hormuz hot, Islamabad Round 2 collapsed: War Day 54 ends with Operation Epic Fury in a peculiar equilibrium: the air war paused (no confirmed US/Israeli strikes on Iranian territory since 8 PM ET Apr 7), the ground war in Lebanon frozen by a fraying second-generation ceasefire, diplomatic tracks broken on both the Iran and Lebanon files, and the maritime domain the sole live combat zone — now accelerating. Trump's indefinite extension buys time but cedes nothing; the blockade is the very leverage Iran calls an act of war. Three US carrier strike groups are converging on CENTCOM (Lincoln in the northern Arabian Sea, Ford in the central Red Sea off Jeddah, Bush transiting the Horn of Africa) signaling Washington is preparing for a potential second round even as it negotiates. Markets read de-escalation; the Apr 22 Hormuz incidents suggest markets may be ahead of the ground truth. The two most consequential indicators to watch over the next 72 hours are (1) whether Iran attempts to escalate maritime seizures into a Touska-scale direct clash with the US Navy and (2) whether the May 1 War Powers deadline forces an administration reckoning with Congress that the Islamabad track has failed to pre-empt. Pope Leo XIV's Africa tour wraps Apr 23; Pakistan's mediation bandwidth remains the key non-kinetic variable.

strike_notes: Day 54 (Apr 22): The sharpest maritime escalation since the blockade began — IRGC opened fire on three commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz and seized two of them hours after Trump extended the Iran ceasefire indefinitely. Iran statement: 'Disrupting the order and safety of the Strait of Hormuz is our red line.' Follows Apr 20 USS Spruance (DDG-111) interdiction of Iranian-flagged M/V Touska in the Arabian Sea (Marines from 31st MEU rappelled from USS Tripoli helicopters and took the ship). FM Araghchi Apr 21 called the Touska seizure and broader blockade 'an act of war and a material breach of the ceasefire'; UN Amb. Iravani filed a formal protest letter with SecGen Guterres. CENTCOM tally (NPR Apr 21): 28 commercial vessels turned back since Apr 13 (up from 27 Apr 20). No UNSC resolution adopted Apr 21-22; Russia and China previously vetoed the Bahrain-drafted Hormuz resolution on Apr 7. Trump's indefinite ceasefire extension (~16:22 ET Apr 21 Truth Social) explicitly maintained the naval blockade; Islamabad Round 2 collapsed after Iran declined to attend. Ghalibaf adviser Mahdi Mohammadi called the extension 'a ploy to buy time for a surprise strike... continuation of the siege is no different from bombardment and must be met with a military response.' MSC and Greek operator both had AIS off at interception — a detail highlighted by CBS News analysts as evidence of anticipated maritime risk.

Senior MP Alireza Salimi told Tasnim that fees 'are currently being deposited into a unified account and the treasury,' with toll amounts varying by cargo and risk level. Some transit fees have reportedly been paid in Chinese yuan. The announcement converts the previously informal IRGC 'Tehran Tollbooth' into a formal, institutionalized revenue stream — a structural escalation of Iran's Hormuz sovereignty claim.

Iranian FM Araghchi arrived Islamabad in the evening; the White House confirmed Special Envoy Witkoff and Jared Kushner depart for Pakistan Apr 25 for direct US-Iran talks 'intermediated by the Pakistanis,' though Iran's FM spokesman publicly denied a meeting is scheduled. Trump-brokered Israel-Lebanon ceasefire was extended 3 weeks Apr 23, but mutual violations continued — IDF killed 6 Hezbollah fighters in Bint Jbeil and 2 civilians in a Touline air strike; Hezbollah shot down an Israeli drone. UN Human Rights Office said attacks on civilians in Lebanon/Israel 'may amount to serious violations of international humanitarian law.' Markets priced higher probability of de-escalation: S&P 500 (7,165.08) and Nasdaq (24,836.60) closed at all-time records; Brent settled $105.33 after intraday touching >$106. UMich final April consumer sentiment 49.8 came in above preliminary but still the lowest on record. NYT investigation said U.S. has expended >1,200 Patriots, ~1,100 stealth cruise missiles, and >1,000 Tomahawks during Epic Fury (WH disputes). The Apr 25-27 weekend Witkoff/Kushner-Araghchi negotiation is the single most consequential diplomatic inflection point of the war.
timeline_data_point: Day 56 — 3 carriers in CENTCOM; Araghchi in Islamabad; Lebanon truce +3 wks; S&P record

event_description: IRGC: 'No intention' of unblocking Strait of Hormuz: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps stated on its Telegram channel: 'Controlling the Strait of Hormuz and maintaining the shadow of its deterrent effects over America and the White House's supporters in the region is the definitive strategy of Islamic Iran.' Deputy Parliament Speaker Ali Nikzad (per Mehr) added that under an order from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, Hormuz will 'under no circumstances' return to its previous state. event_description: Iran offers Hormuz-for-blockade-lift deal, postpones nuclear talks: Via Pakistani mediators, Iran transmitted a written proposal to the U.S. to extend the ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the U.S. lifting its naval blockade of Iranian ports — explicitly deferring nuclear-program negotiations to a later phase. Two regional officials and a U.S. official confirmed receipt. White House spokesperson Olivia Wales: 'These are sensitive diplomatic discussions and the U.S. will not negotiate through the press... never allowing Iran to have a nuclear weapon.' Trump told reporters Saturday: 'Interestingly, immediately, when I canceled it, within 10 minutes, we got a new paper that was much better,' adding Iran 'offered a lot but not enough.' The bypassing of nuclear concessions is widely read as removing Trump's leverage, making acceptance unlikely.
timeline_source: Axios (primary, Apr 27) / Bloomberg / AP via Fortune / CNBC / Al Jazeera live blog

event_description: HASC hearing: Hegseth, Caine, Hurst testify on Iran war: First congressional testimony by Sec. of Defense Pete Hegseth since the war began. Acting Pentagon Comptroller Jules Hurst pegs cumulative Operation Epic Fury cost at ~$25 billion (mostly munitions). Hegseth says any Iran-specific supplemental request will be 'less than $25 billion.' Hegseth calls congressional Democrats and 'some Republicans' the 'biggest adversary' the U.S. faces. Heated exchange with Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) over economic costs ('Your $25 billion number is totally off. It's incompetence'); with Rep. Seth Moulton (D-MA) over a War of 1812 blockade analogy. Hegseth identifies 14 critical munitions for replenishment incl. Patriot, THAAD, SM-3, SM-6, AMRAAM, JASSM, PrSM. FY2027 Pentagon budget request: $1.5 trillion. The $25B figure creates the dashboard's largest single discrepancy with the prior ~$51.85B midpoint.

event_description: Trump rejects Iranian proposal in Axios phone interview: Trump tells Axios in a phone interview that he has rejected the Iranian peace offer that would lift the U.S. blockade and reopen Hormuz while deferring nuclear talks. 'They want to settle. They don't want me to keep the blockade. I don't want to [lift it], because I don't want them to have a nuclear weapon.' Trump describes the blockade as 'somewhat more effective than the bombing.' 'They are choking like a stuffed pig.' Says Iran's oil storage and pipelines 'are getting close to exploding.' The interview hardens the U.S. position published earlier via Rubio Apr 27 and the Apr 25 Pakistan-trip cancellation.

event_description: War Powers Resolution 60-day deadline reached; Trump admin claims war 'terminated': Friday, May 1 marks the statutory 60-day mark from Trump's March 2 War Powers notification to Congress. A senior administration official told AP that 'the hostilities that began on Saturday, Feb. 28 have terminated' for purposes of the 1973 War Powers Resolution, citing the April 7/8 ceasefire — an interpretation Brennan Center counsel Katherine Yon Ebright called 'a sizeable extension of previous legal gamesmanship,' arguing nothing in the WPR's text or design supports a pausable clock. Defense Secretary Hegseth told the Senate Armed Services Committee on Apr 30 that 'we are in a ceasefire right now, which in our understanding means the 60-day clock pauses or stops.' House Speaker Mike Johnson told NBC News: 'I don't think we have an active, kinetic military bombing… right now we are trying to broker a peace.' Senator Susan Collins (R-ME) joined Democrats voting in favor of the latest War Powers resolution, which the Senate rejected on Apr 30; she said the deadline 'is not a suggestion; it is a requirement.' Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) said she will introduce an AUMF when the Senate returns from recess the week of May 11 if the White House does not submit a credible plan. Sen. Mike Rounds (R-SD) said he expected Trump to seek the statutory 30-day extension. Congress began a week-long recess. No Democratic lawsuit has been filed as of publication.
timeline_source: AP/Washington Times May 1; CBS News May 1; CNN Politics May 1; Washington Post May 1

PROJECT FREEDOM launches: US Navy begins 'guiding' commercial ships through Strait of Hormuz: CENTCOM, at Trump direction, commences Project Freedom 04 May with stated objective to 'restore freedom of navigation.' Force package: 2 guided-missile destroyers entering Persian Gulf, 100+ land/sea-based aircraft, 15,000 service members, multi-domain unmanned platforms. CENTCOM: 'not an escort mission' per US official; framed as 'humanitarian gesture.' First two US-flagged merchant vessels successfully transit. Adm. Brad Cooper: 'Our support for this defensive mission is essential to regional security and the global economy as we also maintain the naval blockade.' Trump rejected CENTCOM's more aggressive 'forced-entry' plan presented 30 Apr in favor of calibrated approach. RoE updated to authorize strike on 'immediate threats.' First sustained US-Iran direct kinetic engagement of indefinite-extension ceasefire period.

Iran strikes UAE for first time since 8 Apr ceasefire — Fujairah Oil Industry Zone in flames; ADNOC 'Barakah' tanker hit by drones: Iran launches first major attack on UAE since ceasefire: drone strike ignites fire at Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (VTTI facility) — endpoint of Habshan-Fujairah pipeline (1.5 Mb/d capacity), UAE's only Hormuz-bypass crude export route. 3 Indian nationals moderately injured. Empty ADNOC crude tanker 'Barakah' hit by 2 drones in Hormuz. UAE MoD intercepts 12 ballistic missiles, 3 cruise missiles, 4 UAVs (4th cruise missile fell to sea). event_description: Iran launches Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) — institutionalizes Hormuz tolls and permits: Iran via Tasnim/IRIB officially launched PGSA with email info@PGSA.ir, requiring vessels to submit a 'Vessel Information Declaration' (ownership, crew nationalities, cargo, voyage plan) and receive transit permits, reportedly with tolls reaching $2M/vessel (UNVERIFIED quantum). Statement attributed to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei calls for 'using the leverage of closing the strait' as part of 'a strong Iran' regional order. US Treasury OFAC FAQ confirms such payments unauthorized for US persons. Maritime law experts say it violates UNCLOS transit-passage principle. Lloyd's List notes only ~40 vessels crossed the strait the entire week ending May 3 vs. 120/day pre-war. Most consequential structural event of the cycle: Tehran is converting wartime control over Hormuz into a permanent permit-and-toll regime.

Authorities urged residents to stay clear of debris. Cumulative since war start: 551 ballistic + 29 cruise + 2,263 drones engaged (UAE MoD running tally). IRGC has DENIED responsibility for recent UAE attacks (May 5 statement still standing); attribution flagged DISPUTED. Not all confirmed fully intercepted — debris fell in populated areas. Comes day after May 7 Hormuz tit-for-tat exchange between US and Iran.

event_description: Doueir / Harouf / Habboush, Nabatieh district, southern Lebanon: Air strikes — 11 killed (including 2 children), 36 wounded
location_name: Doueir / Harouf / Habboush, Nabatieh district, southern Lebanon
strike_notes: Day 69-70 (overnight May 7→8): Overnight Israeli air attacks killed 11 people including 2 children, wounded 36 in Nabatieh district (Doueir, Harouf, Habboush). Netanyahu (May 7): 'No terrorist is immune' — claimed responsibility for May 6 Beirut killing of Hezbollah Radwan commander Ahmed Ghaleb Ballout. Lebanon-Israel direct talks scheduled May 14–15 in Washington (US official confirmed). Lebanese MoPH provisional uplift expected to ~2,738 killed / ~8,474 wounded in next bulletin (current May 7 19:52 BST: 2,727 / 8,438).

event_description: Strait of Hormuz approaches / south of Chabahar Port: Ballistic and antiship cruise missiles, drones with HE warheads — Per CENTCOM: 'no US assets struck'; Iran claims 'significant damage'
location_name: Strait of Hormuz approaches / south of Chabahar Port
weapon_system: Ballistic and antiship cruise missiles, drones with HE warheads
strike_notes: Day 69-70 (overnight May 7-8): IRGC Navy fired ballistic + antiship cruise missiles + drones with HE warheads at US naval vessels east of Strait of Hormuz / south of Chabahar Port. Per CENTCOM: 'no US assets struck.' Iran claimed 'significant damage.' Tit-for-tat retaliation framed as response to US tanker disablement (M/T Hasna May 6). Three USN destroyers (Mason DDG-87, Truxtun DDG-103, Rafael Peralta DDG-115) transited Hormuz May 7 'under fire' and undamaged per Trump (ABC interview); Trump: Iranian small boats 'completely destroyed.'

event_description: Gulf of Oman: Vessel boarding / seizure (special operation) — None reported
strike_notes: Day 70 evening (May 8 ~22:00Z): IRGC Navy announced seizure of M/T Ocean Koi (oil tanker) in Gulf of Oman, accusing it of 'trying to harm and disrupt oil exports.' Tanker towed to Iranian port. Iran cited Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) framework as legal basis. Falls within Day 71 horizon (Al Jazeera flash after Day 70 data cutoff).

strike_notes: Iran Joint Military Command (May 8) claimed US air attacks on civilian areas of Qeshm Island wounded 10 sailors and left 5 missing aboard an Iranian cargo ship. event_description: Iran's formal MoU response slips past 48-hr Pakistan-channel window: Iran did not deliver its formal response to the US 14-point MoU within the 48-hour Pakistan-channel window flagged May 7-8. FM spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said Tehran is 'still reviewing' the proposal. Daily Pakistan reported (May 9 09:15 PKT) that US and Iranian negotiators 'could resume next week in Islamabad' on a 14-point one-month framework MoU covering Iran's nuclear program, Hormuz de-escalation, and HEU transfer to a third country. Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif said Pakistan has been in contact with both sides 'day and night.' Trump on Truth Social: 'expects to hear very soon' from Iran.
timeline_data_point: MoU response window: SLIPPED; talks may reconvene in Islamabad next week

event_description: Rubio + Witkoff meet Qatari PM Al-Thani in Miami on Iran MoU framework: Sec State Rubio and special envoy Steve Witkoff met Qatari PM Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani in Miami Saturday afternoon to discuss path to one-page MoU ending the war. Per Axios sources, 'Qatar, Pakistan, Egypt, Turkey and Saudi Arabia are working in tandem.' Al-Thani had separately met VP JD Vance in Washington on Friday May 8. Qatar formally backstops Pakistan as primary mediator. Rubio publicly framed the meeting as discussing 'US support for Qatar's defense.'
timeline_source: Axios 2026-05-09; Times of Israel liveblog 2026-05-09; Reuters
timeline_data_point: Rubio/Witkoff/Al-Thani Miami trilateral; Qatar formally backstops Pakistan

event_description: Pezeshkian sets 'lifting blockade' as precondition for Hormuz negotiations: President Pezeshkian, following his disclosed 2.5-hour direct meeting with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei (revealed May 7), publicly stipulated that Tehran will not negotiate Strait of Hormuz arrangements until the US naval blockade is lifted. He warned against 'unrealistic expectations' compromising 'Iran's dignity and independence' and characterized the path forward as 'difficult yet honorable.' Mojtaba Khamenei remains absent from public view since Feb 28 strikes; NYT (4 Iranian officials) reports severe facial/leg burns and difficulty speaking; he reportedly attends meetings via audio.

event_description: Trump-Xi Beijing Summit Day 1 — joint Hormuz + non-nuclear declaration: Xi Jinping personally descended Great Hall stairs to greet Trump and individually greeted a 17-member US business delegation. Xi opened with Thucydides Trap reference. Talks held under Beijing's official framework of 'a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability' — Xi declared Beijing would treat that phrase as guidance 'for the next three years and beyond.' event_description: Senate war powers vote 7th time fails 49-50 — Murkowski flips; House version ties 212-212: Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) flipped to support Sen. Jeff Merkley's war-powers resolution, joining Collins (R-ME) and Paul (R-KY) as Republican defectors; Sen. Fetterman (D-PA) was sole Democrat opposing. War-powers math has tightened to a single vote; one more Republican defection or one Democratic absence flips the outcome. Political ceiling on a Trump kinetic restart now visibly load-bearing.

event_description: Trump says Tuesday strike on Iran was 'an hour away' before postponement: Trump told reporters at the White House: 'We were all set to go… It would have been happening right now' — confirming the strike scheduled for Tuesday May 19 was operationally prepared and stood down only after Qatari Emir Tamim, Saudi Crown Prince MBS, and UAE President MBZ personally asked him to hold off. Trump publicly framed the postponement as 'two or three days' for Iran to reach an acceptable deal (Al Jazeera headline: 'Attack on Iran in two or three days if no deal, says Trump'). Trump added: 'There seems to be a very good chance that they can work something out. If we can do that without bombing the hell out of them, I'd be very happy.' He also called the war 'very popular' and said he does not have 'enough time' to keep explaining its rationale.

event_description: Senate advances Kaine war-powers resolution 50-47 in first procedural win: The U.S. Senate voted 50-47 to discharge Sen. Tim Kaine's war-powers resolution from the Foreign Relations Committee — the first procedural win after seven failed attempts. Four Republicans crossed over: Susan Collins (ME), Lisa Murkowski (AK), Rand Paul (KY), and Bill Cassidy (LA), who flipped for the first time three days after losing his Trump-endorsed primary. Three Republicans were absent (Cornyn, Tillis, Tuberville); the lone Democratic 'no' was John Fetterman (PA). The resolution directs the President to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran absent a declaration of war or specific authorization. A final passage vote is pending. Cassidy: 'Until the administration provides clarity, no congressional authorization or extension can be justified.'

Carry-forward Friday May 22 closes: S&P 500 7,473.47, Dow 50,579.70 record, Brent $103.94, WTI $97.12, AAA national gas $4.552. Late-afternoon news event drove sentiment for Sunday's Asian session: Trump on Truth Social (~17:00 ET): 'An Agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalization between the United States of America, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the various other Countries… Final aspects and details of the Deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly' — characterized as a 'Memorandum of Understanding pertaining to PEACE,' said the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened. Iran FM spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei (state TV / IRIB / IRNA): the framework is a 14-clause MoU providing a 30-60-day window for follow-on negotiations covering ending the war on all fronts (incl. Lebanon), the Strait of Hormuz, the US naval blockade ('US maritime piracy'), release of frozen Iranian assets, and sanctions relief — nuclear program explicitly NOT in the initial MoU. strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. event_description: Trump in Situation Room: 'blockade will now be lifted'; Iran denies deal: President Trump entered the White House Situation Room for a 'final determination' on the tentative 60-day US-Iran ceasefire-extension MOU. He posted his demands on Truth Social (Iran never to have a nuclear weapon; Hormuz immediately open with no tolls; mines removed/detonated; enriched 'nuclear dust' unearthed and destroyed with the IAEA; 'no money will be exchanged, until further notice') and announced the US naval blockade 'will now be lifted' and stranded ships 'may start the process of heading home.' Iran's foreign ministry publicly rejected: 'we are focused on ending the war, and there are no negotiations on the nuclear issue.' Speaker / chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf: 'we have no trust in guarantees or words — only actions are the measure.' Per ABC, any deal needs Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's approval. The agreement remains UNSIGNED as of the May 29 close.

strike_notes: Day 121 (June 28): the IRGC fired ballistic missiles and drones at Ali Al Salem Air Base (Kuwait) and US 5th Fleet facilities in Bahrain in retaliation for the June 26-27 US strikes on Iranian territory. Kuwait intercepted 2 ballistic missiles (no damage); a Muharraq residential building's top floor was destroyed (no deaths). The IRGC claimed 8 US military sites were struck; a US official said no intended targets were impacted. Bahrain's FM called it a 'dangerous escalation.' A Qatari national was killed at sea by shrapnel during this window (Qatar MoI; cause NOT formally attributed to either US strikes or Iranian drones) plus 1 injured (stable). Coordinates point to the Bahrain (Muharraq) impact site. DAY 129 UPDATE (July 1-6): NO new Iranian retaliation. This June 28 salvo remains the LAST Iranian kinetic action of the war — the June 29 US-Iran stand-down held for the entire July 1-6 window with no new IRGC ballistic-missile or drone strikes on US bases or Gulf states, and no confirmed Houthi attacks on shipping. Iran issued only verbal warnings (a 'decisive/swift response' over any Hormuz miscalculation; 'harsh and regret-inducing responses' if attacked during Ayatollah Khamenei's state funeral) but took no kinetic action; indirect US-Iran talks in Doha (July 1-2) made 'positive progress' and are set to resume ~July 11. DAY 137 CORRECTION: the 'last Iranian kinetic action' framing above is OBSOLETE — the ceasefire collapsed Jul 7 when Iran fired on 3 Hormuz-area tankers, and successive Iranian missile/drone waves hit US assets in Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan, Oman and Qatar plus a Kuwaiti offshore oil platform and 2 UAE tankers over Jul 7-14 (see Jul 7-14 entries). Iran claimed strikes on '80+/85 US sites'; CENTCOM reported NO US casualties; most IRGC battle-damage claims remain unverified.

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

event_description: Bushehr: Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant (perimeter and auxiliary buildings)

event_description: Bandar Abbas: IRIN naval base
casualties_reported: Unknown (earlier phases); 8 Iranian Air Force/Navy personnel killed at Bandar Abbas & Bushehr (Iranian Army, Jul 8)
strike_notes: Key Strait of Hormuz control point. Continuous strikes to suppress coastal batteries. Day 14: Continued strikes on remaining coastal defense positions as part of Strait of Hormuz suppression campaign. CENTCOM reported that within 48 hours of war start, all 11 Iranian warships in the Gulf of Oman had been denied presence. Three commercial ships struck by suspected Iranian projectiles in the strait on March 11. Day 23: Aerial campaign continues (Day 4) with A-10 Warthogs and Apache helicopters. Day 24 (Mar 23): One person killed and one wounded in Bandar Abbas from attack targeting Persian Gulf Broadcasting Center radio transmitter. Day 87 (May 25, Memorial Day): CENTCOM 'self-defense' strikes near Bandar Abbas — most significant U.S. kinetic action inside Iran since the April 8 ceasefire. Targets: Iranian missile launch sites, Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines, and an Iranian SAM site. U.S. official described scope as 'very small'; Iran's Mehr news agency said the situation 'was under control.' Explosions also reported near Sirik and Jask. ENDS 16-day zero-kinetic streak (Days 71-86). CENTCOM framed strikes as defensive and not a ceasefire violation. Day 90 (May 28): overnight US strike on an IRGC drone ground-control station near Bandar Abbas International Airport; US shot down 4-5 Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, with the station reportedly about to launch a fifth (see dedicated entry 2026-05-28-bandarabbas-gcs). DAY 137 UPDATE (Jul 8–14): repeatedly struck in the renewed campaign; on Jul 12 the first-ever US combat sea-drone strike (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) hit the submarine/ship-maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (CENTCOM/USNI/Breaking Defense). Ghadir-class midget submarine imaged on a gantry at the struck pier (CENTCOM video). Civilian fishing docks ('Panj Pleh') hit by shrapnel per resident accounts (IranWire).

location_name: Saudi Aramco — Jizan refinery & Yanbu oil installations, Saudi Arabia
strike_notes: FIRST HOUTHI STRIKE ON SAUDI OIL FACILITIES SINCE 2022 (spokesman Yahya Saree). Jizan: a large smoke plume and a NASA FIRMS thermal anomaly at ~01:17 UTC confirm a fire at the 400,000 bpd refinery; Saudi Arabia and Aramco issued no official damage or casualty assessment. Yanbu: 2 ballistic missiles were intercepted by a Patriot battery operated by the GREEK military in Saudi Arabia, with no damage reported. STRATEGIC SIGNIFICANCE — Yanbu is Saudi Arabia's primary Hormuz-bypass corridor, handling ~92% of Saudi seaborne crude exports in June 2026 (Kpler/AFP), with loadings hitting a record 4.7M bpd around Jul 13 (Signal Ocean); the strike demonstrates the Houthis can reach it. SEQUENCE — Jul 22: Houthis struck the Saudi tanker Encelia (bow fire confirmed by SPA) and claimed the Layla (unconfirmed). Jul 24: the Saudi-led coalition struck Houthi targets in Hodeidah and on Kamaran Island (2 injured, per Al Masirah). Jul 25: these Aramco strikes, in retaliation. Jul 26: Houthis claimed 'two qualitative operations' on the Red Sea coast, and Saudi Arabia downed Iranian-backed Iraqi-militia drones aimed at petroleum facilities. DAY 168 (Aug 14): Houthi forces again targeted Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery in the Red Sea / Bab-el-Mandeb corridor, one of the supply-side headlines cited in the Aug 14 oil rally (TradingEconomics).
